About the job

Tether is seeking a Blockchain Expansion Manager to drive strategic growth initiatives across Tether’s blockchain partner ecosystem. This role sits within the Blockchain Expansion function and focuses on building and managing high-impact relationships with blockchain foundations while executing strategic projects that expand the real-world adoption and utility of Tether assets.

The Blockchain Expansion Manager will work closely with blockchain partners to design and deliver initiatives that meaningfully grow Tether’s asset usage through practical, real-world use cases. This role requires strong partnership management skills, strategic thinking, and the ability to execute complex projects across multiple internal and external stakeholders.

This is a hands-on role suited to someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment, operates with autonomy, and brings structure and rigor to high-impact growth initiatives.

  • Manage and deepen strategic relationships with blockchain foundations and ecosystem partners.
    Act as the primary point of contact for assigned blockchain partners, ensuring alignment between partner objectives and Tether’s strategic priorities.

  • Design and execute high-impact growth projects in collaboration with blockchain partners to drive adoption of Tether assets through real-world use cases.

  • Think strategically about how Tether can work with blockchain ecosystems to create scalable, sustainable projects that expand asset usage and circulation.

  • Coordinate and manage cross-functional initiatives involving regional expansion, economics, marketing, and other internal teams.

  • Track, manage, and report on project progress, outcomes, and effectiveness, ensuring initiatives deliver against defined objectives.

  • Identify opportunities to improve execution efficiency, project structure, and partner outcomes.

  • Operate with a high degree of autonomy, taking initiative to identify new opportunities and drive them forward.

  • Support internal leadership with clear updates, insights, and recommendations based on partner and project performance.

Job requirements

Mandatory

  • Proven experience in partnership or ecosystem management, ideally within crypto, fintech, or technology.

  • Strong track record of managing high-impact, strategic growth projects from concept through execution.

  • Excellent organisational skills with a high level of attention to detail.

  • Ability to track, manage, and optimise multiple initiatives simultaneously.

  • Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to translate ideas into executable projects.

  • Experience working cross-functionally with teams such as expansion, economics, marketing, or product.

  • Ability to work autonomously, take initiative, and operate effectively in a remote, global environment.

  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

Preferred

  • Experience working with blockchain foundations or Layer 1 / Layer 2 ecosystems.

  • Familiarity with stablecoins, blockchain infrastructure, or real-world blockchain use cases.

  • Experience operating in fast-growing or unstructured environments.

The opportunity

Stripe works with the world's most ambitious platforms, marketplaces, and enterprises building the next generation of financial products — and the scale of what they're building creates an extraordinary opportunity to go deeper. As these users expand into new markets, launch AI-powered products, and layer embedded finance onto their core offering, the topics that unlock their next phase of growth become increasingly strategic: design a monetization strategy that captures full value, price competitively across geographies without eroding margin, structure go-to-market motions and sales enablement for white-labelled financial products, and translate Stripe's capabilities into durable revenue streams for their business. 

This role exists to meet that moment — bringing a more prescriptive, hands-on advisory approach to the users where commercial model design is the primary lever for growth, and ensuring that Stripe's most strategic relationships are supported not just with best-in-class infrastructure, but with the monetization and revenue strategy expertise to make the most of it.

What you’ll do

As a strategy & transformation advisor for growth & monetization, you will own and build Growth & Monetization sub-practice end-to-end. You will be the globally recognised expert in this space working directly with and advising some of Stripe’s strategic users and in process enabling your teammates to do the same. Your work will sit at the intersection of commercial strategy, product economics, and payments infrastructure — and will span five core advisory domains:

 

1. New Revenue Channel Growth & Discovery

Work with platforms, marketplaces, and enterprise users at the earliest stages of their thinking to identify, validate, and prioritise new revenue channels. This includes embedded finance, monetization of distribution, bundled value-added services, and adjacency expansion. You will bring structure, data, and commercial rigour to decisions that are often made on instinct.

2. AI Product Pricing Strategy

SaaS companies are racing to launch AI-powered features and products — and most are flying blind on pricing. You will develop a repeatable advisory model that helps users design pricing architectures for AI products: usage-based vs. seat-based vs. outcome-based models, packaging strategy, willingness-to-pay research, and competitive positioning. This is a fast-moving space and an area where Stripe can take a distinctive, opinionated stance.

3. Platform & Marketplace monetization on Stripe

Stripe powers some of the world's most sophisticated platforms and marketplaces. You will help existing and prospective platform users unlock the full commercial potential of their Stripe integration — including but not limited to buy-rate modelling, revenue share to interchange-plus transitions, merchant segmentation and tiered pricing, and product-to-commercial-model fit across Connect, Terminal, Money management products (Capital, Treasury, Issuing), and Billing. You will draw on and extend the existing monetization Strategy capability & offering.

4. Geographic Expansion & Payments monetization

As users expand into new markets, their payments economics change significantly. You will advise on how monetization models need to evolve across card mix, scheme fee structures, local regulation, and competitive pricing dynamics in new geographies. The output will be clear market-entry pricing strategies, multi-year margin models, and phased expansion plans.

5. Embedded Finance & Digital Assets monetization

As platforms increasingly embed financial products into their core offerings, monetization strategy becomes one of the most complex and consequential decisions they face. This advisory domain covers the full spectrum of Money as a Service (MaaS) products: how platforms, marketplaces, and vertical SaaS companies can design and price the financial products they embed — including payments acceptance, card issuing programmes, treasury and money-movement capabilities, working capital and lending facilities, and stablecoin or crypto-native infrastructure. You will help users build monetization models that capture the full economic value of their embedded financial stack, advising on revenue share structures, margin stacks, product bundling, and the commercial trade-offs between depth and scale across each financial product category. This domain spans both traditional fiat rails and emerging digital asset infrastructure, and is relevant wherever a platform is moving beyond pure SaaS economics into financial services revenue.

  • Establish Stripe as having a distinctive, opinionated position on growth and monetization in our target verticals and segments.
  • Track and report sub-practice performance: pipeline contribution, closed Professional Services revenue, NPS, and user outcomes.

  • Partner with Account Executives and Solutions Engineers to position the capability as a differentiator in competitive deals.

Global enablement

  • Develop training programmes, playbooks, and certification paths for the ProServ team to deliver foundational Growth & Monetization advisory.
  • Serve as an internal escalation point and thought partner for complex monetization questions arising from any strategy & transformation engagement worldwide.

Product and market intelligence

  • Collaborate with Stripe's Product and Engineering teams to inform product roadmap decisions based on user monetization needs and gaps.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. About the team

Brand Studio sits at the center of everything Stripe shows the world — from visual identity and brand systems to campaigns, events, digital experiences, and global marketing. The studio functions as a creative multiplier: setting the standards, building the systems, and producing the work that helps Stripe show up with intention and quality across every touchpoint.

World-class creative output requires world-class operational infrastructure. Brand Operations is the function that makes Brand Studio's work possible at scale — not by managing the execution, but by architecting the conditions that enable it. That means shaping what enters the studio, ensuring clarity before a brief is written, and building the systems that allow creative directors and producers to focus on what they're here to do: create exceptional work.

What you’ll do

Most operations leaders are brought in to fix problems. We're looking for someone who prevents them — and designs the system in which prevention becomes the norm.

The Head of Brand Operations exists upstream from creative execution. This role's job is to ensure the work entering Brand Studio is strategically aligned, clarified, prioritized, resourced, and fully prepared for delivery before it ever reaches a creative director or producer. It also means ensuring the company understands how to work with Brand Studio — what it takes to be a ready partner, and where a given initiative stands on the roadmap. When that infrastructure is working, creative leaders spend their time and energy on the thing they're actually here to do.

This role lives at the altitude of setting the team up for success. That means the early-stage, ambiguous conversations where partners are still forming ideas — where the business need hasn't been articulated, where the biggest risks and opportunities haven't been named, and where a structural decision will compound over time. It means building and maintaining a roadmap the entire company can see and trust. And it means leading a team of producers who own their projects fully, with your role being the system that makes their ownership meaningful.

This role isn't about staying out of the details entirely — it's about not defaulting to them. You'll roll up your sleeves when the moment calls for it. But your primary value is in designing the ecosystem, not running the work. If you want to build the system in which great work consistently becomes possible — and watch it scale — this is a rare opportunity to do that.

Responsibilities

  •  Architect the Brand Studio ecosystem. Engage cross-functional partners — Marketing, Product, Comms, PMM — before briefs exist. Turn ambiguous asks into clear, sequenced workstreams so creative leaders inherit clarity, not chaos.
  • Build and maintain the Brand Studio roadmap. Sequence and prioritize work based on business importance, creative opportunity, and team capacity. Give leadership a forward-looking view of what's coming — and the tradeoffs involved.
  • Set the conditions for great work. By the time a project reaches a creative director or producer, the business need is defined, stakeholders are aligned, and the problem is framed. Creative leaders shape the work. You shape the environment that makes the work possible.
  • Own and evolve the operational infrastructure. Build the intake processes, alignment frameworks, and communication rhythms that help Brand Studio run at scale. Refine them as the team grows.
  • Make how Brand Studio works visible to the company. Partners should be able to find the roadmap, understand where their project stands, and know what it takes to show up ready. The process of working with Brand Studio shouldn't require a meeting to explain.
  • Run the business of Brand Studio. Own the budget, manage agency and external production partnerships from procurement through delivery standards, and partner with Finance on clear accounting structures. Give the team the resources and partnerships it needs to deliver.
  • Lead, develop, and set the cultural tone. Hire great people, build their judgment, and set clear ownership. Give direct feedback, delegate fully, and create the stability that lets people do their best work. You're a steward of how this team shows up — the norms, the standards, and what it means to operate at this level.
  • Stay attuned to what's forming. Brand-level initiatives take shape before briefs exist. Catch early signals across the company and help shape ambiguous ideas into clear outcomes before they reach the studio.
  • Represent Brand Studio at the leadership level. Keep senior leaders informed on priorities, direction, and impact. Make the case for what deserves investment, what should wait, and why.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 12+ years of experience in brand operations, creative operations, or creative program management. A track record of building operational systems at the function level, not just executing inside them.
  • 5+ years managing a team of producers, program managers, or operations professionals, with clear evidence of developing talent and building production capability.
  • Demonstrated experience engaging cross-functional partners before briefs are written — shaping workstreams, clarifying business needs, and setting creative teams up to succeed.
  • Experience building and owning an annual creative roadmap for a team or function, including prioritization frameworks, capacity planning, and tradeoff communication with senior leadership.
  • A track record of building operational infrastructure — intake processes, prioritization systems, partner communication frameworks — that scaled and outlasted your direct involvement.
  • Experience managing significant budgets, including developing transparent accounting structures in partnership with Finance.
  • Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to align competing priorities and influence without authority across a large, cross-functional organization.
  • People management instincts that build team judgment rather than dependency — genuine delegation, direct feedback, and a consistent bias toward developing others over personal execution.
  • Experience incorporating AI into team workflows and driving measurable adoption across a creative or operations team.

Preferred qualifications

  •  Experience inside a world-class in-house creative studio or brand team, with deep familiarity with the full creative production lifecycle — from strategy and concept through final delivery.
  • A track record of building or rebuilding a brand operations function from scratch within a company or team at scale.
  • Experience managing global creative agency and external production partnerships end to end — from procurement and onboarding through creative direction and delivery standards.
  • Deep understanding of how brand, marketing, and product teams operate at a technology company, with the instincts to bridge creative ambition and business priorities.
  • Experience building operational transparency systems — roadmaps, dashboards, or partner-facing communication frameworks — that gave an entire organization real-time visibility into a creative team's capacity and priorities.
  • Experience building creative process standards, playbooks, or partnership guidelines that became lasting institutional infrastructure.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

One of the company's most important strategic priorities is to build great products and experiences for Enterprises—and we are at an inflection point in the growth of our Enterprise business, with significant momentum.

The Enterprise team is responsible for ensuring all of Stripe's products and services best fit the unique needs of global, modernizing enterprises. Our Enterprise Product extends beyond our APIs and dashboards—to Enterprise executive engagement, our perception in the market, our partner ecosystem, how we collaborate with our users to bring them live, and our users' day-to-day interactions with our GTM and support teams—they're all part of the Product experience for these users.

We focus on expanding and innovating on Stripe's platform in ways that help the largest and most complex customers run their businesses. Our work is highly cross-functional—partnering with almost every other team at Stripe—to execute on the priorities that matter most to Enterprises and ensure that they are successful on Stripe.

What you'll do

As a member of the Enterprise Strategy and Operations team, you'll build the infrastructure, processes, and organizational muscle to help our Enterprise business scale:

Responsibilities

  • Lead cross-cutting company strategy projects and collaborate with teams to implement changes
  • Partner with multiple stakeholders across Enterprise and other Stripe teams (e.g., product teams, marketing, sales, support) to achieve the goals of the Enterprise Engine Catalyst. You'll need to objectively evaluate teams' competing priorities and align stakeholders on the optimal solution for Stripe and our users
  • Partner directly with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to accelerate progress, develop new operating models, and incubate new programs
  • Establish new operating models in collaboration with key cross-functional teams, focusing on roadmap development and context alignment
  • Coordinate annual and long-range planning efforts across teams contributing to the Enterprise segment, and drive alignment with partner teams to ensure a cohesive approach to planning
  • Drive projects, timelines, and commitments on internal projects and customer deliverables

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

  • 7+ years of experience in strategy and operations, product strategy, product management, or similar roles at technology companies, including highly cross-functional work spanning strategy, product, analysis, and operations in a fast-paced environment
  • Critical thinking and first-principles thinking (e.g., ability to question how we work rather than simply executing), and the ability to zoom out to the most important questions
  • Strong program management skills with experience managing end-to-end execution of projects and programs that have transformed their company's operations and delivered quantifiable business impact
  • Excellent written and verbal communication with the ability to speak to leaders across different teams, such as partnerships, product, engineering, and sales
  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in influence without authority environments, execute with minimal guidance, and operate in contexts with a high degree of ambiguity

Preferred qualifications

  • Payments ecosystem or Enterprise software experience
  • Ability to build trust and partner with senior leaders

  • Comfort with SQL or constructing dashboards and structuring advanced data analysis to measure program success

About the Organization

The Core Infrastructure organization operates the foundational systems that power Stripe globally — including databases (MongoDB, PostgreSQL), high availability and disaster recovery (HADR), AWS cloud infrastructure, Linux servers, container orchestration, mesh networking, service discovery, and network edge infrastructure.

Within Core Infra, the Regional Enablement Platform (REP) team helps Stripe launch and operate new regions without learning about broken dependencies from users. REP builds the regionalization, validation, deploy-safety, and operator tooling needed to answer practical launch-readiness questions: can critical payment paths run from the new region, which services still depend on a remote control plane, what breaks under packet loss or failover, and what must be fixed before deploys, launches, traffic shifts, or failovers proceed. The team uses traffic replay, synthetics, failover drills, dependency analysis, CI/CD gates, and incident data to turn those findings into platform fixes, service-owner asks, and reusable readiness checks across networking, HADR, and service teams.

This role is based in Bangalore and serves as a senior technical anchor for Core Infrastructure in India, with direct cross-region influence across AMER, EU, and APAC.

What you'll do

As a Staff Engineer on REP, you will play a key leadership role in enabling Stripe's infrastructure to power all of our products, globally and at scale. You will decide how Stripe validates that a new region can safely take traffic and continue working through network loss, failover, and deploy changes. You will define the checks that must pass before launch or failover, build validation systems that replay real production paths against regional infrastructure, and turn those checks into CI/CD gates, operator workflows, and concrete fixes for service or platform owners. You will also help build Core Infrastructure's senior technical bench in Bangalore through design review, mentoring, and cross-region technical leadership. 

Responsibilities

  • Define evidence-based readiness criteria for regional launches, traffic migrations, and failovers — replacing manual checklists with repeatable, globally consistent patterns

  • Security mindset: A great portion of our product is trust. While we have a dedicated security team, every engineer brings security to their designs from the start.

  • Review Card Network Releases: Review, analyze, and assess biannual card network releases to identify key initiatives that will significantly impact Stripe’s business. Collaborate cross-functionally with various teams to ensure proper visibility and prioritization of these initiatives. At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. Through our crypto solutions for financial institutions, businesses, governments and developers, we are improving the global financial system and creating greater economic fairness and opportunity for more people, in more places around the world. And we get to do the best work of our career and grow our skills surrounded by colleagues who have our backs. 

If you’re ready to see your impact and unlock incredible career growth opportunities, join us, and build real world value.

THE WORK:

Ripple is building the Internet of Value: infrastructure that moves money as fast as information moves today. Every payment that flows across our network passes through real-time financial crimes controls: sanctions screening, wallet risk analysis, transaction monitoring, and travel rule compliance. The Financial Crimes Engineering team builds and operates that layer.

This is the engineering that determines whether payments clear or hold, whether Ripple meets its regulatory obligations across jurisdictions, and whether the network can scale without compromising on compliance. The problem space is genuinely hard: high-throughput distributed systems, real-time decisioning, multi-source coordination across external compliance data providers, regulator-grade audit trails, and resilience.

As a Staff Software Engineer on this team, you'll set technical direction for that platform. You'll own the architecture of the compliance control plane: the vendor-agnostic, resilient, provable system that lets Ripple move value without moving financial crime, and you'll drive its evolution across Ripple's product lines. This is a role for someone who operates beyond individual services: you'll define the technical strategy others build against, anticipate where the platform needs to go before it's asked, and raise the engineering bar across the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Set architectural direction for the compliance control plane: real-time screening orchestration, the resilience and observability layer, vendor-agnostic integration, and the decision/data plane, designing for where the platform needs to be across future jurisdictions and product surfaces, not just today's requirements
  • Drive the hardest, highest-ambiguity technical problems end to end: multi-vendor failover, sub-second decisioning under load, regulator-grade auditability, and resilience across partial dependency failures
  • Translate evolving regulatory obligations and organizational goals into durable engineering primitives and a sequenced technical roadmap, with milestones and clear execution plans
  • Anticipate platform risks and scaling constraints before they become incidents, and lead the initiatives that address them
  • Partner directly with senior leaders to align complex cross-functional objectives and shape how regulatory requirements become engineering reality
  • Set standards for production ownership: observability, alerting, incident response, and raise the reliability bar for the whole team
  • Mentor senior and mid-level engineers, elevate design quality across the team, and act as a technical multiplier: the engineer whose presence makes everyone around them better

WHAT YOU'LL BRING: 

  • 8+ years building production backend systems, with deep expertise in Java (or comparable JVM languages, Go, Rust)

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and demonstrated ability to work independently, analyse problems and data sets to make complex investigation decisions
  • Self-disciplined, diligent, proactive and detail oriented

About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Platform

Our Platform organization’s purpose is to enable Gemini to scale effectively and empower our engineering teams to focus on building innovative financial products and experiences for individuals around the world. Platform focuses around building a scalable and secure foundations platform, enabling Engineering to deploy, validate, and operate their services in production, improve resiliency of the service and increase organizational efficiency by reducing operational toil and increase system efficiency through architectural evolution.

The Platform team engages directly with our other engineering teams to onboard them onto our platform systems, reviewing and recommending design and architectural decisions, and guiding our engineering teams on how to implement the tooling provided by the larger Platform organization required to ensure systems can scale and react to changing conditions, with continuous improvement loops.

The Role: Senior Data Platform Engineer

As a Senior Data Platform Engineer, you'll be an SRE for our data infrastructure: responsible for the reliability, automation, and operability of the database and datastore fleet, not just tuning any single engine. You'll work closely with data engineering and product engineering teams to build self-service, automated foundations that let teams provision, scale, and operate their own datastores safely.

Your role centers on deep relational database expertise (PostgreSQL, Aurora) - internals, replication, failover, backup/recovery, and query performance - paired with the automation and tooling to run that expertise at scale rather than by hand. You'll extend that same automation-first discipline to the other datastores in our fleet - NoSQL/document, columnar, key-value, and streaming systems - so that scaling, failover, and provisioning are repeatable and largely self-service. You'll drive improvements to observability, incident response, and uptime posture through proactive ownership of the platform, and you'll bring SRE practices (SLOs, error budgets, toil reduction, blameless postmortems) to how we run data infrastructure.

This role is ideal for someone who thinks in systems and automation first, thrives on cross-team collaboration, and wants to reduce operational toil across a diverse set of database technologies in a fast-paced, cloud-native environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Automation and Reliability Engineering: Build Infrastructure as Code (IaC), CLI tools, and CI/CD-driven automation that make database provisioning, scaling, failover, and deployment self-service, consistent, and repeatable across environments - this is the core of the role, not a supporting activity.
  • Database Scaling and Optimization: Serve as the team's depth on relational database systems (e.g., Amazon Aurora, PostgreSQL) - replication topologies, failover, backup/recovery, and query/engine-level performance - ensuring high performance and availability under growing workloads.
  • Fleet-Wide Infrastructure Design: Extend that operational rigor to the rest of the datastore fleet - document, key-value, and columnar systems - applying the right paradigm to the right workload and building common tooling and guardrails across all of them.
  • High Availability, Observability, and SRE Practice: Define and track SLOs/error budgets, build proactive monitoring and alerting, implement high-availability architectures, and participate in the on-call rotation to troubleshoot and resolve production issues quickly.
  • Pipeline Integration: Collaborate with data and product engineering teams to integrate with upstream and downstream pipelines - both real-time and batch - via message queues (e.g., Kafka), ETL workflows, and processing frameworks.
  • Performance Tuning and Troubleshooting: Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks at both the query and infrastructure levels across engines. Establish alerting, observability, and incident response procedures that reduce MTTR and maintain service health.
  • Toil Reduction and Operational Excellence: Continuously identify and automate away repetitive operational work; contribute to shared documentation, incident retrospectives, and platform playbooks to improve team effectiveness and reliability of operations.

Qualifications:

  • 5 years of experience in the field.
  • Deep, specialist-level experience managing and scaling relational databases - cloud-native systems like PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora, or similar - including replication, failover, backup/recovery, and query/engine performance tuning.
  • Demonstrated SRE mindset: experience building automation, self-service tooling, and guardrails that eliminate manual, repetitive database operations rather than performing them by hand.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one non-relational paradigm in production (e.g., NoSQL, columnar, document, key-value), and working knowledge of when to apply each.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based data platforms and services such as AWS RDS, Redshift, EMR, Google BigQuery, or Databricks.
  • Experience in an infrastructure as code environment (Terraform), developing automated solutions to solve support and operational issues.
  • Proficiency writing scripts, CLIs, or services that increase developer productivity and reduce operational toil, in languages like Python, Go, etc.
  • Understanding of CI/CD, observability tooling, SLOs/error budgets, and incident response in production environments.
  • Experience integrating with data pipelines and real-time messaging systems like Kafka or Kinesis.
  • Comfortable participating in on-call rotations and owning uptime and recovery responsibilities across multiple database technologies.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills; able to work effectively across infrastructure, data, and product teams.

  • Competitive starting pay

  • Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant
  • Comprehensive health plans

The Developer Experience and Product Platform (DEeP) organization empowers all of Stripe's products with a shared product platform that delivers high-quality, consistent, cross-product experiences across our UI and API surfaces. DEeP focuses on providing a scalable developer experience that any developer can leverage to accelerate a customer's ability to create value from Stripe.

Within DEeP, the Extensibility program is how Stripe expands its total addressable market and increases customer retention. With extensibility, Stripe becomes programmable — customers and product teams can adapt Stripe to their needs on a common platform.

Stripe has three interconnected extensibility primitives.

  • Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).
  • Custom Objects — User-defined data models (e.g., Shipments, Locations, Warranties, Entitlements) with first-class APIs, SDKs, and Dashboard experiences.
  • Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.

These primitives are deeply interdependent, involve 10+ cross-functional teams, and culminate in a flagship product launch.

What you'll do

We're seeking a product-focused Technical Program Manager to drive the Extensibility program across the Workflows, Custom Objects, and Scripts workstreams. This is a newly created, high-impact role at the intersection of platform engineering, product management, and cross-organizational program ownership.

In this role, you'll own one of the most strategically consequential programs in DEeP — driving the direction, health, and outcomes of Stripe's Extensibility platform across Scripts, Custom Objects, and Workflows. You'll set the program strategy in partnership with DEeP leadership, holding organizations accountable to the success of the program.

  • Drive cross-org decisions across DRIs in Script Platform, Custom Objects, Apps, SDK, Observability, DevEx, and Versioning — actively resolving the hard, ambiguous integration and ownership questions that fall between team boundaries.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Financial Crimes Team at Robinhood works across multiple verticals to protect our customers and ensure strict compliance with all relevant Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Sanctions regulations. As our team of passionate professionals continues to evolve the program, we are intensely focused on leveraging innovative thinking, advanced analytics, and cutting-edge technology to build a best-in-class Financial Crimes Program.

As the Senior Specialist, Model Validation & Analytics, you will play a key role in this mission by executing the validation, testing, tuning, and optimization of various transaction monitoring and filtering programs across Financial Crimes. You will partner closely with the AML Surveillance Team, engineering partners, and cross-functional verticals to ensure our financial crimes models and systems are accurately implemented, rigorously evaluated, and effectively calibrated to meet the diverse regulatory requirements of our domestic and international lines of business.

This role is based in our Denver, CO, New York, NY, or Westlake, TX office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Model Validation & Review Execution: Perform independent, rigorous quantitative and qualitative analyses of rule-based and machine learning financial crimes surveillance models, filtering systems, and detection logic targeting model design, algorithm soundness, data integrity, and change management
  • Technical Review & Remediation: Act as a technical bridge within a fast-paced fintech environment by leveraging a solid foundation in data engineering, data modeling, and infrastructure. Collaborate seamlessly with software engineers, data engineers, and data scientists to decipher complex logic, evaluate model implementations, test data pipelines, and support the remediation of model issues.
  • Optimization & Model Tuning: Execute effective tuning methodologies and statistical analyses to continuously calibrate and enhance surveillance models. Work on strategic initiatives focused on maximizing risk detection capabilities while systematically reducing false positive volumes to ensure an efficient and effective alert review process.
  • Logic & Data Integrity Assurance: Conduct comprehensive data validation and logic testing initiatives to establish a strong foundation of data quality. Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and end-to-end reliability of critical data pipelines and inputs feeding our compliance models, mitigating systemic risks and safeguarding the integrity of our transaction monitoring ecosystem.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as a knowledgeable subject matter resource in AML and Model Risk, providing practical domain insights and supporting cross-functional partners in understanding model logic, performance, and risk trade-offs.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Build strong working partnerships across engineering, product, and compliance teams to ensure technical solutions are conceptually sound, effective, and aligned with our risk tolerance.
  • Change & Issue Management: Uphold change and issue management policies for covered systems, models, and solutions, ensuring end-to-end traceability and maintaining defensible documentation for internal audit and external regulators.
  • AI Strategy & Tech-Forward Adoption: Bring hands-on capabilities and experience leveraging AI tools, Large Language Models (LLMs), and automation techniques to enhance daily productivity, elevate deliverable quality, and optimize team workflows.
  • Documentation & Reporting: Author thorough, concise, and defensible validation reports, change and issues management documentation, and executive summaries that clearly explain model theory, testing logic, performance findings, and actionable recommendations for key stakeholders.

 

What you bring

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in a quantitative, technical, or financial field (e.g., Computer Science, Data Analytics, Statistics, or Finance)
  • Experience: 5+ years of experience across AML, Financial Crimes, or risk management within the financial services or fintech industry, with a focus on model validation, quantitative analysis, or surveillance system management.
  • Domain Expertise: 3+ years of direct experience in the verification, validation, testing, or tuning of AML rule-based systems and/or machine learning models, along with a working knowledge of core Model Risk Management (MRM) principles and governance standards.
  • Technical & Analytical Skills: Proficiency in SQL and experience using quantitative tools or programming languages (e.g., Python, R) to query large datasets, perform statistical analyses, and evaluate model performance.
  • Adaptability & Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical and quantitative concepts to non-technical partners, coupled with an ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow revenue, and unlock new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet. There is an enormous amount of work ahead, and an opportunity to do some of the most meaningful work of your career.

About the team

The Funded Startups team partners with the most promising venture-backed startups across EMEA. We combine deep knowledge of Stripe’s products with strong relationships across the startup ecosystem to help founders build, monetize, and scale their businesses globally.

Our work brings the next generation of high-potential businesses to Stripe and helps them create sustainable growth—directly advancing Stripe’s mission to increase the GDP of the internet.

What you’ll do

As an Account Executive on the Funded Startups team, you will build partnerships with some of Italy’s most innovative and fast-growing venture-backed startups. You will help founders and operators understand how Stripe’s financial infrastructure can support their growth ambitions, unlock new revenue streams, and create an advantage in their markets.

You will own a high-velocity sales motion from prospecting through close, while developing a strong understanding of each user’s business, technical environment, and priorities. You will identify opportunities for users to adopt more of Stripe’s product suite, create and execute campaigns that build new pipeline, and partner cross-functionally to set users up for long-term success.

Responsibilities

  • Identify and qualify high-potential venture-backed startups through inbound leads and proactive outbound prospecting.
  • Own the full sales cycle, from first engagement to closing
  • Build and execute territory and account plans that drive new business, product adoption, and sustained user value.
  • Develop a deep understanding of users’ business models, technical environments, and pain points; recommend the Stripe solutions that best meet their needs.
  • Create pipeline through research, networking, targeted outreach, cold calling, and territory campaigns.
  • Represent Stripe in the Italian startup ecosystem and help expand our local presence through founder, investor, and community engagement.
  • Develop and work with a network of international and local Parters 
  • Partner with the Investment Partnerships team on venture-capital portfolio analysis and founder-focused events.
  • Collaborate with in-country go-to-market teams and our Dublin headquarters on shared initiatives and regional events.
  • Coordinate with Solutions Architects, SDRs, Marketing, Product, Risk, Operations, and other partners to deliver a seamless user experience.
  • Bring user feedback and complex needs to internal teams to help improve Stripe’s products and go-to-market approach.
  • Deliver a thoughtful, high-quality experience in every interaction, regardless of deal size.

Who you are

You are a strategic, commercially minded seller who enjoys building trusted relationships and operating with pace. You can manage high-velocity deal cycles while navigating technical conversations and coordinating a diverse set of internal stakeholders.

You are curious about ambitious businesses and the problems they are solving. You combine strong sales judgement with a solution-oriented mindset, adapt quickly in ambiguous environments, and take ownership of moving work forward. You are motivated by helping founders build and scale, and by developing your own craft along the way.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification. The minimum requirements are the baseline for consideration; preferred qualifications are a bonus.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in a closing sales role; comparable experience in a product-focused commercial role will also be considered.
  • Professional fluency in Italian and English.
  • Experience working with venture-backed startups in Italy, with an established network across founders, investors, accelerators, and the broader Italian startup ecosystem.
  • A track record of consistently achieving or exceeding ambitious sales targets.
  • Experience managing a full sales cycle in a complex or technical environment.
  • Ability to understand technical ecosystems and build credibility with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical judgement and the ability to manage multiple priorities across complex sales cycles.
  • Experience building territory plans that identify the highest-impact activities and opportunities in a market.
  • Experience leading cross-functional projects and coordinating input from a range of internal teams.
  • Strong relationship-building skills with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability and motivation to succeed in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

Preferred qualifications

  •  Experience in payments or financial technology.
  • Experience in a sales or customer-facing role at a high-growth technology company.
  • Experience working with venture-backed startups in Italy, with an established network across founders, investors, accelerators, and the broader Italian startup ecosystem.
  • Interest in business models, monetization, and the challenges of scaling a company internationally.

You'll be exposed to new ideas, emerging technologies, and complex challenges that push you to stay at the top of your game while helping scale products and infrastructure used by tens of millions of users and thousands of developers across the web3 ecosystem. You'll join a network of builders that reaches the edge of our ecosystem. Consensys alumni have moved on to become tech entrepreneurs, CEOs, and team leads at tech companies.

About PODS Team

People and Talent support the members of our Consensys community. We strive to be the destination employer of choice for our ecosystem. That goal is embedded in all the work we do to attract, retain and support our incredible talent.

PODS — People Operations, Data & Systems — is the infrastructure layer behind everything our People team does — the systems, data, and operational processes that make it possible to hire, pay, onboard, develop, and support people at scale. When this function works well, it's invisible. When it doesn't, everyone notices.

We're looking for someone to take ownership of our core People systems. In this role, you will be the primary subject matter expert on ADP Workforce Now and the broader HR technology ecosystem, the person Finance calls when People data doesn't match, the person Legal calls when they need audit evidence, and the person the People & Talent team relies on for system builds, enhancements, and troubleshooting.

What you’ll do

HRIS administration and system integrity 

You are the technical owner of ADP Workforce Now and the PODS technology ecosystem. System health, configuration, data integrity, and day-to-day administration are yours — not tasks you contribute to, but outcomes you own.

  • Platform ownership — Manage day-to-day ADP WFN configuration, security roles, workflows, custom fields, and system health. You know where everything is, why it's set up the way it is, and what breaks if it changes.
  • Business process design — Take business needs from requirements through configuration, testing, and post-launch validation — end to end, without handing off. When a stakeholder brings you a problem, you translate it into a working system solution and own it through to adoption.
  • Product releases — Own configuration, testing, and rollout of new ADP product releases and system enhancements. Proactively flag opportunities to simplify or automate existing processes before problems surface.
  • Integration management — Own all system integrations across payroll entities, benefits carriers, finance tools, and core HR platforms — both automated API connections and manual data flows. Monitor, troubleshoot, and escalate when things break.
  • Security and access — Manage role-based access across HR systems, enforce least-privilege standards, and maintain SOX-ready access review evidence on a defined cadence.
  • Vendor management — Own day-to-day vendor relationships across the stack — performance accountability, escalation paths, SLA tracking, and contract awareness. Not just ticket submission.

Technical project ownership and process automation  

You lead technical workstreams from intake through completion — representing the People Operations perspective on systems, data, and integration projects across the organization.

  • Technical project ownership — Own HR systems and data projects end to end — scoping, configuration, testing, rollout, and documentation. You represent PODS interests in cross-functional projects and ensure the People Operations perspective is built into technical decisions, not bolted on afterward.
  • Process automation — Systematically replace manual, error-prone workflows with automated processes. Use AI-assisted tools to rapidly prototype and build People Operations automations — turning process ideas into working solutions on fast, business-critical timelines. Measure the reduction in manual effort and error rates over time.
  • SOX and compliance — Maintain documented controls, gather and organize audit evidence, and partner with Legal and Finance to ensure People systems meet compliance requirements at every stage.
  • Change management — Test before deploying. Document after deploying. Communicate to stakeholders before either. Every system change has a testing plan, a rollout plan, and a runbook.

Data management and stakeholder enablement 

You are the check-and-balance for People data across the organization — and the person who makes that data accessible and understandable to the people who depend on it.

  • Data governance — Establish and maintain data definitions, quality standards, field ownership, and retention policies. When two stakeholders get different answers to the same question, you are the reason that stops happening.
  • Reporting and analysis — Prepare, review, and analyze People data and reports. Build custom reports and executive-facing dashboards in ADP and connected tools. Translate outputs into clear, actionable information for Finance, FP&A, Legal, and People leadership.
  • Audits — Run recurring data audits, maintain audit logs, and ensure evidence is organized and retrievable. Catch discrepancies before they reach stakeholders.
  • Documentation and training — Maintain up-to-date process documentation and deliver training materials for new system enhancements. Build genuine self-service capability in the HR team — reducing the ad hoc support load over time.

Operational support  

You provide timely, effective support for daily system needs and cyclical operations — and you use patterns in that support to build lasting fixes rather than repeat the same interventions.

  • Employee and manager support — Provide responsive support for system questions, access issues, and ad hoc requests. Identify recurring patterns and build runbooks or automations to address root causes.
  • Cyclical operations — Own the systems side of open enrollment, compensation cycles, re-orgs, payroll close, and year-end processes. These run on a schedule — they need to run without heroics.
  • Vendor relationships — Hold vendors accountable to SLAs, manage escalations above the support queue, and keep contract renewal dates on the radar.

Would be great if you brought this to the role

  • Deep functional expertise in ADP Workforce Now — you have configured workflows, built reports, managed security roles, and troubleshot integration failures as a hands-on administrator, not as an end user
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in HR systems administration, HRIS configuration, or HR technology operations
  • A track record of business process design end to end — you've taken requirements from a stakeholder conversation through configuration, testing, launch, and post-launch validation without handing off
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business needs into working system solutions — you ask the right questions, design the right solution, and build it
  • Experience with process automation and AI-assisted tooling — you've used modern tools to prototype and build automations that eliminated meaningful manual effort, and you can point to the results
  • Strong data management instincts — you've built custom reports, run data audits, caught data quality issues before they became business problems, and you understand what governance actually means in practice
  • SOX or audit compliance experience — you understand what controls mean, what evidence looks like, and what an auditor will ask for
  • Project management capability — you've managed a high volume of requests and shifting priorities without losing track of what matters most, and you communicate status without being asked
  • Intellectual curiosity and sound judgment — you ask why something works the way it does, and you know when to move fast and when to slow down and think
  •  A bias for action paired with resilience in ambiguity — you've operated in fast-moving environments where requirements changed mid-project and you didn't wait for perfect information to make progress

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role.

The Core Infrastructure team's mission is to build and evolve the foundational platform that every Robinhood engineering team builds on — owning the systems, primitives, and developer-facing abstractions that power 24/7 trading, crypto, and global expansion. We treat infrastructure as a product: reliable, fast to provision, and invisible to the teams above it.

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer on Core Infrastructure, you will own the architectural evolution of three deeply interconnected domains: service mesh and connectivity, compute platform, and infrastructure provisioning. Your decisions will directly shape engineering velocity, operational reliability, and Robinhood's ability to expand to new regions and markets. This is not an operations role — it's a once-in-a-platform-lifecycle opportunity to redesign the foundation before complexity becomes permanent!

This role is based in our Menlo Park, California office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

  • Own service mesh architecture end-to-end — standardize and evolve Robinhood's Istio and Envoy deployment, eliminate deprecated communication patterns, and build the networking foundation for multi-region operation
  • Drive Kubernetes compute platform evolution — define the long-term direction for cluster lifecycle, scheduling strategy, control plane architecture, and multi-region resiliency across Robinhood's entire compute fleet
  • Redesign infrastructure provisioning — transform Terraform from a collection of ad-hoc configurations into a scalable, self-service platform capability that enables rapid region provisioning and developer autonomy
  • Operate with source-level depth — diagnose and resolve issues at the Kubernetes API machinery, etcd, Envoy xDS, and Terraform provider layer, and contribute upstream where it serves the platform
  • Define technical direction across teams — produce architecture proposals, lead design reviews, and drive cross-functional alignment on infrastructure decisions that affect every engineering organization at Robinhood

What you bring

  • Deep, hands-on expertise with Kubernetes internals — API server, controller reconciliation, etcd watch propagation, scheduler mechanics, and admission control
  • Deep working knowledge of Istio and/or Envoy at the source code level — including the xDS API as a protocol; experience debugging at the control-plane/data-plane boundary
  • HTTP/2 and gRPC wire-level knowledge — connection management, flow control, stream multiplexing, and observability
  • Terraform at architectural scale — module design patterns, provider internals, remote state management, and multi-region provisioning
  • Production Go or Python for infrastructure tooling; strong fundamentals in writing well-structured, tested, operationally sound code
  • Proven ability to drive cross-functional architectural change across large or complex engineering organizations — influencing without authority and shipping durable decisions

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership
  • Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account for expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more!

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Security Incident Response team works to analyze, investigate, and respond to threats before they impact Stripe’s business or users. From external attacks to insider threats, our goal is to respond with speed and precision, remediate, and support the incident postmortem process. The team is distributed, working across multiple AMER time zones, and will regularly coordinate with stakeholders in EMEA and APAC.

What you’ll do

You will leverage your security engineering experience to improve incident response capabilities at Stripe. With an emphasis on user and entity behavior analytics, as well as endpoint hardening, you will gain a deep understanding of Stripe’s systems, tooling, and workflows to be able to differentiate between legitimate and malicious activity.  Using both threat intelligence and collected telemetry, you will guide and build Stripe-specific signals enrichment logic and incident response solutions that scale with our company.  Lastly, your analytic capabilities will be critical during security incidents to reduce uncertainty, uncover root causes, and inform future prevention and detection mechanisms. 

Responsibilities

  • Analyze and investigate a broad range of threats or activities occurring on client devices
  • Develop requirements for detection models and enhancements to existing systems
  • Collect, transform, and ingest raw data from disparate sources into threat detection pipelines
  • Streamline incident response capabilities, ensuring the tooling and processes are clear
  • Work cross-functionally with security engineering and data science teams to build solutions for analyzing security events data at scale and protecting Stripe networks, systems, and data from threats
  • Provide actionable insights to help identify, prevent, detect, and respond to anomalous or potentially malicious user and entity activity
  • Act as the subject-matter expert and primary contact for stakeholder teams invested in Security Analytics and Detection programs as well as Stripe-wide security initiatives
  • Collaborate effectively with teammates, leading projects, mentoring others, and developing and championing quality standards within the team

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 3+ years experience analyzing large data sets to solve problems and/or building models with a behavioral approach to security
  • B.S. or M.S. Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience
  • Expert knowledge of Python and SQL, and familiarity with other programming languages
  • Existing experience with log analysis (e.g. first or third party applications, system / data access, event logs), network security, digital forensics, and incident response investigations
  • Proficiency with developing and using novel analytical methods to build, automate, and improve detection and response systems
  • Ability to communicate results clearly and focus on impact

We’re looking for a Research Engineer to build the intelligent systems that power Antimetal. You’ll prototype new approaches, run experiments, and own the path from research to production. You’ll work closely with platform and product to shape agent capabilities and contribute to evaluation methodology.

Infrastructure, and its corresponding observability, is a hard domain to model. Telemetry is high-volume, noisy, and ephemeral. Ground truth is approximate. We’re building AI agents that understand this complexity and can reason about what’s happening, why, and how to fix it, including making changes to code and configuration.

Research Areas

Infrastructure Intelligence: Models that help us understand what’s happening in infrastructure and why. Detecting anomalies, forecasting issues, analyzing telemetry across logs, metrics, events, and traces, understanding causality, and connecting runtime behavior back to code. These capabilities form the foundation our agents use to reason about infrastructure.

Autonomous Agents: Long-running, parallel agents that detect, diagnose, and remediate infrastructure issues, including fixing code and configuration. Advancing multi-step reasoning, orchestration, context management, memory, and reinforcement learning.
Evaluation: Making sure agents work well and informing how we improve. Partnering with platform to build evaluation methodology, generate synthetic data, analyze historical incidents, and model the domain.

About the Role

Hyperbolic is looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Supply Operations Manager to support the day-to-day operations of our growing GPU supply network.

This role will own the operational relationship with our existing infrastructure suppliers, from contract administration and payment reconciliation to recurring supplier check-ins and issue resolution. You will work closely with our Supply, Finance, Legal, Engineering, and Product teams to ensure supplier agreements are accurately executed, invoices are properly reconciled, and operational commitments are consistently tracked and fulfilled.

Beyond execution, you will help design the systems, processes, and sources of truth that allow our supply operations to scale. As our supplier network grows, the structure you build will determine how efficiently we grow with it.

This is a role for someone with exceptional attention to detail. You will be responsible for managing contracts and payments involving significant financial commitments, and small errors can have meaningful operational or financial consequences. The ideal candidate is rigorous, dependable, proactive, and comfortable creating structure in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Do

Contract and Commercial Operations

  • Manage the operational lifecycle of supplier contracts, order forms, amendments, renewals, and related documentation.

  • Review executed commercial terms against company standards, and ensure key obligations, including pricing, contract dates, payment terms, service-level commitments, notice periods, and termination provisions, are accurately recorded, tracked, and flagged when they deviate from our standards.

  • Maintain a centralized and reliable source of truth for all active supplier agreements.

  • Coordinate with Legal, Finance, and Supply leadership to ensure contracts are properly reviewed, signed, and implemented.

  • Proactively flag upcoming renewals, payment deadlines, notice periods, and contractual risks.

Invoice and Payment Reconciliation

  • Review supplier invoices against contracted rates, actual capacity delivered, uptime, service credits, and usage data.

  • Investigate discrepancies involving billing periods, GPU counts, hourly rates, downtime, credits, deposits, and other charges.

  • Identify service credits owed to Hyperbolic under supplier SLAs and ensure they are claimed and recovered.

  • Partner with Finance and internal technical teams to validate invoice accuracy before payments are approved.

  • Maintain clear reconciliation records and ensure outstanding discrepancies are resolved promptly.

  • Track deposits, prepayments, recurring payments, true-ups, credits, and other supplier-related financial obligations.

Supplier Relationship Management

  • Own the ongoing operational relationship with existing suppliers.

  • Lead biweekly supplier check-ins and prepare clear agendas, updates, action items, and follow-ups.

  • Track open issues related to capacity delivery, maintenance, billing, performance, support, and contractual obligations.

  • Ensure internal and external owners are aligned on deadlines and next steps.

  • Build strong, professional relationships with supplier operations, finance, sales, and technical teams.

  • Escalate material risks or unresolved issues to the appropriate internal stakeholders.

Systems and Operational Coordination

  • Coordinate supplier onboarding, capacity handoffs, testing windows, and operational readiness.

  • Partner with Engineering to track infrastructure performance, downtime, maintenance, and other issues that may affect billing or supplier commitments.

  • Design and maintain repeatable workflows, templates, dashboards, and documentation that make supply operations more scalable and less dependent on any single person.

  • Identify gaps in existing processes and proactively implement improvements.

  • Provide regular reporting on supplier health, contractual obligations, invoice status, and unresolved risks.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated ability to manage complex information without losing accuracy.

  • Experience reviewing contracts, invoices, pricing terms, or financial reconciliations.

  • A systems mindset: you don't just complete tasks, you build the process so the task runs better next time.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to identify inconsistencies, ask the right questions, and escalate issues appropriately.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced startup environment where processes are still being developed.

  • High level of ownership: you follow issues through to resolution rather than simply handing them off.

  • Proficiency with spreadsheets and the ability to work confidently with pricing, usage, and payment data.

Nice to Have

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

The Marketing team at Polymarket is responsible for telling the world what Polymarket is, why it matters, and why trading here is better than reading a poll. We work across growth, brand, comms, and product, and we move fast because the news moves fast. This role sits at the center of that operation: the connective tissue between what Product is building and how the rest of the company talks about it, ships it, and grows from it.

As Product Marketing Manager, you'll help craft go-to-market motion for Polymarket's product. That means helping shape the product and new feature launches: the positioning, the channel plan, the briefs, the timeline, and the readout afterward.

This is a high-ownership role with real surface area. You'll touch new market verticals, trading mechanics, mobile onboarding, rewards, and anything else Product ships.

What You'll Do

  • Own the GTM launch calendar end-to-end, keeping feature definitions, launch briefs, and ship dates current so Product, Marketing, and Comms always know what's coming, when, and who owns what.

  • Work with product to bring competitive intel and audience insight into decisions before they're finalized.

  • Write positioning and messaging for new features and market verticals, from one-liners and messaging hierarchies to copy direction for social, email, push, and in-app surfaces.

  • Help build and execute channel plans for each launch, working across Growth, Design, and Comms to make sure the right message hits the right audience at the right moment.

  • Track launch and campaign performance, report clearly on what worked and what didn't, and feed those learnings back into the product team and the next launch playbook.

  • Run post-mortems after major launches and translate findings into repeatable process improvements that make the next launch faster and sharper.

  • Compress full launch plans into short sprints when breaking news or live events demand it, without cutting corners on clarity or brand consistency.

What We're Looking For

  • Has owned at least one B2C go-to-market launch end-to-end, from positioning and channel plan through cross-team coordination and post-launch readout.

  • Writes sharp, specific product messaging. Can take a complex mechanic and produce a one-liner a first-time user understands in five seconds, then defend every word choice with user evidence.

  • Proven cross-functional operator who keeps Product, Design, Growth, and Comms aligned without becoming a bottleneck or a meeting adder.

  • Comfortable with speed. Has examples of compressing a multi-week plan into a short window around a live moment, and doing it without brand or compliance missteps.

  • Experience writing competitive positioning based on real market and user research, not instinct alone.

  • Strong written communicator. Launch briefs, messaging docs, and performance readouts are all part of the job, and they need to be clear enough that everyone acts on them.

  • (Plus) Genuine interest in news, sports, politics, or markets. Understands at a gut level why people trade on what they believe.

  • (Plus) Experience running event-driven marketing tied to live sports, elections, or breaking news moments.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Partner closely with engineering and data science on knowledge-base quality, and with sales and customer success on what's closing, where deals stall, and what drives adoption.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

Strong product retention and net revenue retention — proof the product is genuinely good, not just sold. Time from sign-on to a customer actively using the product and getting value drops materially, proving the motion scales rather than bottlenecking on hand-built rollouts. A growing roster of recognizable logos — Interlochen and beyond — publicly running on the product.

The measure isn't purely shipped features. It's whether the enterprise product motion is a real, compounding thing that exists because you built it.

Compensation

Competitive base salary and meaningful early-stage equity, reflecting the ownership this role carries. We'll be transparent about the full picture in our first conversation.

Who We're Looking For

Experience

  • ~7+ years in product, with senior end-to-end ownership of a product line or surface

  • Owned a roadmap and been accountable for outcomes (adoption, retention, growth), not just shipping

  • Shipped a product where simplicity or ease-of-adoption was the core challenge

  • Has driven real AI/product adoption inside large organizations, not just shipped a pilot

  • Worked closely with engineering and data science on a technical product, without needing the infrastructure translated

The Stuff That's Harder to Teach

  • Roadmap and sequencing judgment. You can turn a vision and a pile of market signals into a plan where each build sets up the next. Without this, a team ships well but doesn't get anywhere.

  • Product taste. Our whole bet is consumer-simple feel over hard infrastructure underneath. You relentlessly cut toward effortless rather than defaulting to feature-completeness — this is the rarest, least teachable thing we're hiring for.

  • Real discovery instincts. Not running calls for their own sake, but hearing something you didn't already believe and changing course because of it.

  • Backbone, delivered as consensus, not decree. You push back on vision — and on engineering's default architecture — when the market or the product disagrees with it. You get there by asking the right questions and bringing people along, not by declaring "do it this way."

  • Product thinking over process. You're organized because it drives value to customers fast, not because a granular plan feels like progress. You'd rather write a direction doc that lets the team generate its own tickets than write every ticket yourself.

Bonus (Genuinely Not Required)

  • Consumer or prosumer product experience where ease-of-adoption was the whole game

  • Product shipped to large-enterprise or Fortune 500 buyers

  • Founder or early-stage operator experience

  • A 0-to-1 product built, not only scaled

Why This, Why Now

edisyl is at the moment where the technology is proven and the enterprise market is ready. We're building a genuinely new product surface, and scaling raises the bar for a coherent, compounding roadmap and sustained market discovery. That's the backing to invest in dedicated product ownership now, so growth is pointed at a deliberate plan rather than a series of strong individual releases.

Right now, that ownership doesn't exist. You'll be the one who builds it.

Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.
