Jito's engineering team has already rebuilt how it works around AI, and the gain in output is real. Everywhere else in the company, that same gain sits uncaptured. This role exists to go get it, with a company-wide mandate from day one.

Jito builds the market layer of Solana. We run the validator client behind a majority of the network's stake, JitoSOL, BAM, and JTX. About 40 people. Ops, legal, finance, marketing, business development, and product each have well-understood, expensive workflow problems that a strong engineer could solve in a week, and today those problems sit unowned or get picked up as side work.

You would be the first dedicated AI engineer at Jito Labs.

We're a small team with product-market fit. That means:

  • High ownership: every team member drives significant technical decisions and shapes our roadmap.
  • Fast execution: we ship rapidly and iterate based on real-world feedback. Progress, not motion.
  • High quality bar: the details are the product. We don't trade them for speed.

About the Position

You'll work with the CEO and with teams across the company to find the highest-leverage work. Some of that is problems people already know they have. Much of it is optimization they've stopped noticing, in processes that function well enough that nobody has questioned them. This role owns the cross-cutting investments no single team will prioritize, and builds for the teams that can't build for themselves.

The default is to buy and configure where something off the shelf does the job, and to build where nothing does. Everything you ship carries a named maintainer and clear criteria for when to sunset it.

A meaningful part of the role is spent with the people doing the work, engineers included, in enough depth to understand where their time actually goes. From there you scope it, build it, secure it, roll it out, and keep it running.

Security owns the platform layer. You own the applications built on top of it, in partnership with Security from design time forward.

This is a mid-to-senior individual contributor role, roughly three to five years of experience. It is not a research or model-training position.

Reports to the CEO.

What Makes This Hard

  • The surface area is the whole company. Every team has a different workflow, a different data shape, and a different tolerance for a tool that gets it right most of the time. Doing this well means understanding how Jito actually runs, team by team, including the optimizations that people inside a process have stopped seeing.
  • Buying is usually correct and rarely sufficient on its own. Finding the seam between configuring a vendor and building it yourself is most of the judgment this role requires.
  • Adoption is a people problem before it's an engineering one. The strongest model users at any company are well ahead of the median, and closing that distance takes teaching and documentation as much as code.
  • Security and speed pull against each other, constantly. We are infrastructure that validators and stakers depend on, and we take that seriously, so anything touching internal data gets designed with Security from the start. Judging where the extra week is worth spending, and where it isn't, is a large part of this role.

    • What We're Looking For

  • Three to five years shipping and operating production services. You can stand up VM sandboxes, MCP servers, and vendor LLM integrations, and you'll pass an engineering screen.
  • LLM and agent tooling you've shipped that people use today. We'll ask who uses it and how often. Prototypes nobody adopted won't clear the bar.
  • Buy-first instincts with the range to build. You can explain your last custom build and why it was necessary, and you've sunset projects of your own.
  • The ability to sit with someone in Legal, Finance, or Marketing, extract the real workflow, and ship something they use every week, without a PM translating for you.
  • Judgment about which teams are actually drowning, and the restraint to avoid pushing tools on people who didn't ask.
  • Security at design time by reflex, with constraints treated as parameters of the design.
  • You think like an operator. The most interesting problem and the highest-impact problem are frequently different ones, and you can tell which is which. Getting nerd sniped by a hard technical problem that saves the company an hour a month is the failure mode here.
  • Self-directed prioritization. You surface use cases, estimate their impact, rank them with the CEO, and say no. There is real work waiting on day one, and the expectation is that you find more of it than anyone hands you.
  • Operational ownership. You maintain what you ship, and have clear kill criteria for each project to avoid unnecessary maintenance burden.
  • The prospect of 40 people producing the output of 400 reads as interesting to you.

    • Blockchain experience is not required.

    Relevant Background

    If you have experience in any of the following, you may be a good fit:

  • OpenHands, Langchain or coding agent frameworks, deployed and maintained in a real environment
  • Building and operating MCP servers
  • CLI tooling and automation that other engineers picked up and kept using
  • Security and network operations: identity, secrets management, egress control, sandboxing
  • Connecting existing systems into something that holds up under real use, and recognizing when to write it yourself instead
  • Being the only person in your function at a company under 50 people
  • Owning a vendor surface: spend, data exposure, renewals
  • Rust, Python, TypeScript or a systems background
  • Linux systems and DevOps experience
  • Crypto or Solana literacy

JTX is our trading app, and it runs on the fastest market infrastructure on Solana, which we also built. What nobody has done yet is make that speed something a trader can feel. That is this job.

JTX is live. Two frontend engineers built it to this point and you would be the third. The work now is one to a hundred: harden what exists, make it hold up under real volume, expand onto mobile, and raise the ceiling on every screen a trader touches.

We're a small team with product-market fit. That means:

  • High ownership: every team member drives significant technical decisions and shapes our product roadmap.
  • Fast execution: we ship rapidly and iterate based on real-world feedback. Progress, not motion.

About the Position

You'll own the surface of JTX across web and mobile: order entry, market data, charts, positions, execution quality, onboarding, and the wallet flows underneath all of it.

The role suits a generalist with strong taste. You'll partner with design, product, and the infrastructure team, and you'll make architectural calls that stick for years. If you've spent time thinking about how markets actually work on Solana and want to build the product layer on top of that, this is the role.

Stack: React 19 + TypeScript on Next.js. Jotai + TanStack Query. Tailwind with a token-based design system. TradingView Advanced Charts on our own datafeed. Privy wallets. WebSockets to our engine. Web ships as a PWA; native mobile apps are in development.

  • Shipping volume: three engineers own the entire surface of a live exchange; the backlog is bigger than the team, so throughput and prioritization are part of the job
  • Keeping product behavior and design language consistent between web and mobile while being very attentive to nuances of each mobile platform
  • Making execution quality something a trader can see in a glance instead of something they take on faith

  • Build and own the JTX client across web and mobile
  • Ship real-time trading interfaces: order books, charts, order entry, positions, fill and execution visibility
  • Hit tight latency and render budgets against streaming market data, and decide what belongs on the client versus the server
  • Build wallet and signing flows, including self-custodial and embedded wallet onboarding
  • Own the shared component, state, and data layers the rest of the product team builds on
  • Make architectural decisions that hold as the codebase, the team, and the user base grow by an order of magnitude
  • Ship fast, watch real users, iterate

  • Attention to detail bordering on obsessive. You can look at a screen and say what is wrong with it, and it bothers you until it's fixed.

  • Strong fundamentals: browser performance, memory, websockets, network behavior under load
  • Security-first instincts around signing flows, key handling, and what should never touch a log
  • Comfortable in a codebase that is already live. You can refactor and clean up without stopping shipping.

About us

Solflare is one of the fastest-growing crypto wallets in the world. With around 4 million monthly active users and over $20 billion in digital assets secured through our platform, we’re building a powerful gateway to Web3. Founded in 2021, Solflare now has a team of nearly 150 people, with offices in Zagreb, Belgrade, and Novi Sad, plus remote teams across the globe. Our vision is simple but bold: a world where everyone uses a Web3 wallet and has full control over their assets – achieving true financial independence.

Our culture

At Solflare, we’re on a mission to empower people to truly own and thrive – starting with our own team. We take on bold challenges with curiosity, grit, and a deep sense of accountability. Here, progress means learning fast, solving smart, and showing up for each other without ego. You’ll join a team where we question the status quo, celebrate shared wins, and never settle for “just good enough.” If you’re excited by growth – yours, ours, and society’s – you’ll feel right at home.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior Brand Designer to help evolve how Solflare shows up across campaigns, social media, presentations, events, merchandise, and other physical and digital experiences.

This is a senior, hands on individual contributor role for someone who can turn a brief into a strong creative concept and scalable visual system and execute it to a high standard. Experience with motion is valuable, but deep motion specialization is not required.

You’ll own briefs from concept through delivery and execute most of the work yourself. You’ll also brief and direct freelancers or specialist partners when a project requires additional capacity or expertise.

You’ll report to the Head of Design and work within the Brand & Creative team, partnering closely with Marketing, Product Marketing, Product Design, and Operations. You’ll present your work, actively seek feedback, and contribute a clear point of view to the work of the wider team.

This is not a people management role, a full time art direction position, or a rebrand. Solflare already has a strong identity. Your job will be to extend it intelligently, creating new expressions and systems without losing what makes the brand recognizable. Over time, the role can grow toward greater art direction responsibility while remaining close to the craft.

Core responsibilities: 

Campaigns and brand expression

  • Turn product launches, company initiatives, and marketing briefs into memorable visual concepts and campaign systems.
  • Design creative for web, social media, paid campaigns, app-store assets, presentations, and other marketing channels.
  • Partner with Marketing and Product Marketing to continuously raise the standard of Solflare’s campaigns and social presence.
  • Extend the Solflare identity when new formats or challenges require solutions beyond the existing guidelines.

Digital and motion

  • Translate brand concepts into effective digital and social content.
  • Use motion where it strengthens an idea, either by creating straightforward animations yourself or collaborating with motion specialists.
  • Brief and direct external motion designers when a project requires specialist expertise.
  • Ensure motion work feels consistent with Solflare’s broader brand identity.

Systems and creative quality

  • Build reusable templates, libraries, components, and guidelines that help the team produce high quality work efficiently.
  • Review creative across channels and identify opportunities for stronger consistency, clearer storytelling, and more effective production workflows.
  • Brief and collaborate with freelancers, illustrators, motion designers, and production partners when specialist support is needed.

Events and physical experiences

  • Develop creative concepts for conferences, sponsorships, events, and merchandise that help Solflare stand out online and in person.
  • Design high impact company presentations, internal communications, recruitment campaigns, and employer-brand materials.
  • Prepare production ready artwork, review proofs, and work with vendors to ensure high-quality physical execution.

 

Requirements:

  • At least five years of experience in brand, visual, or graphic design, supported by a portfolio that demonstrates both depth and range.
  • Exceptional craft in typography, composition, hierarchy, and visual storytelling.
  • Experience working within an established identity system and meaningfully extending it not only applying existing templates.
  • Experience applying brand systems across several formats, such as campaigns, digital content, presentations, print, merchandise, or events. We don’t expect you to be a specialist in every area.
  • The ability to take ownership from brief through delivery, challenge unclear or weak briefs constructively, and make thoughtful creative decisions.
  • A collaborative, low ego approach and the ability to give and receive direct feedback.
  • Thoughtful use of generative AI and modern creative tools, with good judgment about where they increase speed and where hands-on craft matters more.
  • Professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

Your portfolio

A portfolio is required. Applications without one cannot be considered.

Please send links rather than attachments and include three to five projects that demonstrate:

  • Exceptional brand and visual-design craft.
  • Experience developing a concept into a coherent campaign or visual system.
  • An identity system you meaningfully extended beyond its original guidelines.
  • Range across relevant digital and physical formats.
  • Your specific role, the constraints you worked within, and the reasoning behind your key decisions.

Motion work is welcome. A small number of well explained projects is more valuable than a large collection of disconnected visuals.

Nice to have

  • Experience creating short form motion for brand or campaign work.
  • Experience briefing or directing motion designers.
  • Experience with After Effects, Rive, Lottie, or similar tools.
  • Experience with 3D tools.
  • Illustration skills that broaden your creative range.
  • Experience working with crypto, fintech, or highly technical products.
  • An interest in Web3, digital ownership, or emerging technologies.

 

Personality traits we value:

  • Problem-solvers: You see roadblocks as opportunities and don’t wait around for someone else to fix things.
  • Self-starters: You take initiative, follow through, and deliver with pride, no excuses, no shortcuts.
  • Team players: You thrive in a “we, not me” culture, lifting others up while sharing the load.
  • Adaptable minds: You embrace change, question how things are done, and constantly look for better ways.
  • Ownership mindset: You own your work end-to-end, communicate openly, and learn from every challenge.

Why Solflare?

  • Make an impact: Your work will directly shape how people interact with and understand crypto wallets, empowering users around the globe.
  • Work with the best: Collaborate with a talented, driven team across design, engineering, and product to build innovative, user-first experiences.
  • Flexibility: Remote or office – up to you. Enjoy a flexible work environment based on trust that supports your well-being and fosters creativity, as well as flexible work time – work when you are most productive, with no micromanagement
  • Perks & benefits: individual education budget, cool team buildings, private health insurance, to name a few
  • Learn about crypto: No crypto experience? No problem! You’ll be part of a team that will teach you the ropes and help you grow into an expert.

Join us at Solflare and be part of something bigger than yourself. We’re not just reacting to trends; we’re building the future. If you’re ready to push boundaries, challenge assumptions, and make an impact, we want to hear from you.

Apply now and help us shape the future of decentralized finance.

Ethena is building the financial infrastructure for the next generation of digital dollars, powered by USDe. As Head of Product, you'll lead Ethena's product organisation end to end — managing and mentoring a small team of Product Managers who each own products across our wider suite, while also taking direct, hands-on ownership of the company's single most strategically important product: a landmark new consumer offering, currently in stealth development, that will be central to Ethena's next phase of growth. Full detail on this flagship product will be shared with shortlisted candidates as part of the interview process.

This is a high ownership role that spans both people leadership and individual-contributor product ownership. On the flagship product, you'll be defining the vision, setting the metrics, and making the calls on a fast-moving initiative you'll help take from near-zero to launch. Across the wider suite, you'll set the standard for product process, coach and develop two Product Managers, and bring consistent rigor and prioritisation discipline to the product organisation as a whole.

You will operate with a very lean team and limited resources across product and dev, standing up much of the function's process from scratch. You'll partner closely with the CEO and CTO, and report directly to senior leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and mentor a team of two Product Managers running products across Ethena's wider suite, setting the standard for process, prioritisation, and quality across the group.

  • Take direct, hands-on ownership of the company's flagship new consumer product (full details shared during the interview process) as its single accountable owner — defining vision, roadmap, and success metrics.

  • Stand up a real but lightweight product operating system from near-zero: discovery, prioritisation, roadmap, spec/PRD standards, decision-logs, and operating rhythm, appropriate for a lean team.

  • Establish scalable processes for support, risk, and compliance, working with legal to navigate relevant regulatory requirements across jurisdictions.

  • Own the product budget and manage outsourced dev and agency relationships for cost-efficiency and quality.

  • Scale the product team and operating culture as the business grows, beyond the initial team of two.

What We're Looking For

  • A history of managing products with over 100K monthly active users.

  • Experienced mentoring, or leading other Product Managers, ideally in a lean or high-growth environment.

  • Have personally led and shipped payments or banking products, and know consumer money products from the inside.

  • Deeply opinionated and evidence-based about how to measure a consumer fintech product and how retail users actually behave.

  • Comfortable operating as a credible peer to founders — able to take over product ownership from a technical founder and earn trust fast, communicating crisply in writing as well as verbally.

  • Hands-on by nature — happy in the detail (writing specs, reviewing flows, digging into data) with minimal resources on both product and dev, rather than only directing.

  • Strong UX judgment and design sensibility for customer-facing platforms with high complexity.

  • A bias toward action, and comfort delivering sophisticated products under ambiguous conditions in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment.

Senior/Staff Software Engineer

Own the backend behind Ethena’s money-movement app — design secure APIs and auth, ensure every payment is correct, and set the engineering bar in this new team.

Role Overview

We're building a new engineering team at Ethena to own a money-movement product built on top of our stablecoin infrastructure. As the Staff/Senior Engineer, you own the correctness and evolution of the money-paths at the core of the product — payments, payouts, deposits, transfers, and reconciliation — and the app-facing APIs and authentication backend the native mobile app depends on.

Your north star: money always moves correctly, exactly once, and observably; and every request the app makes is fast, well-versioned, and secure. This is a senior IC role with real design authority over the backend — you set the standard for how these services are built, not just execute tickets.

Role Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and own complex backend systems for a high usage consumer app.

  • Own the app-facing API contract as a product: versioned, backward-compatible endpoints with client idempotency keys, a consistent error model, and clean pagination, built in partnership with the iOS team.

  • Own the authentication and authorization backend, including the passkey/WebAuthn relying party, session/token lifecycle, and authorization enforcement at every API boundary.

  • Defend the auth surface against abuse through rate limiting, anomaly detection, and secure handling of PII and secrets.

  • Set patterns, tests, and documentation so the backend can be safely extended by any engineer, raising the correctness, testing, and security bar by example and in review.

  • Trace and document money-paths end-to-end, from API through wallet/executor/submitter/indexer, event streams, and on-chain settlement, closing real correctness and reliability gaps as you go.

  • Ship fast, test-first. Deliver on a tight cadence with test-driven and behaviour-driven development — you can prove the correctness of a payout path, not just its happy path.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience building and operating backend systems that move real money in production — payments, exchange/settlement, lending, banking, or crypto — with a track record of preventing (or fixing) idempotency, rounding, or reconciliation bugs.

  • Experience designing and owning client-facing APIs consumed by a mobile app at scale: contracts, versioning and backward compatibility, idempotency keys, error models, pagination, and rate limiting.

  • Experience building or operating an authentication/authorization backend — OAuth2/OIDC, JWT session/token lifecycle, RBAC/ABAC scopes, MFA/step-up — ideally including a WebAuthn/passkey relying party.

  • Hands-on integration with real financial third parties end-to-end (card issuing, KYC/fiat ramp partners, or payments/settlement providers), including their webhooks, failure modes, and reconciliation.

  • On-chain settlement literacy from the backend — nonces, gas, reorgs, RPC failure, confirmation depth — treating chain data as untrusted input.

  • Strong TypeScript (or a fast, credible path from Go/Kotlin/Rust/Java), with Postgres, an event/queue system (NATS/Kafka/SQS-class), and gRPC-based service-to-service communication at production scale.

  • A test-first culture matching ours — BDD/integration testing with real dependencies (Testcontainers-style) — and fluency with agentic development workflows (Claude Code, MCP, skills) as a core part of how you engineer.

Engineering Manager / Tech Lead

Lead a hands-on engineering team at Ethena building a money-movement product: own architecture, hire top engineers, and ship production code with real financial impact.

Role Overview

We're building a new engineering team at Ethena to own a money-movement product built on top of our stablecoin infrastructure. You'll take the technical and people leadership of that team, shaping the architecture, setting the engineering bar, hiring the people around you, and shipping the hardest parts yourself.

This is a hands-on player-coach role, not a hands-off manager seat. While the team is small, you'll spend most of your week writing and shipping production code — you'll be one of the strongest individual contributors on the team, take the most critical work yourself, and review everyone else's. Leadership, architecture, and hiring sit on top of that, not in place of it. As the team grows the balance shifts toward leadership, but coding stays a standing part of the job.

It's a rare combination: the scope and autonomy of an early-stage build — you own the architecture, shape the team, and decide how it works — with the backing, treasury, and distribution of one of the largest companies in stablecoins behind you.

Role Responsibilities

  • Write and ship production code most days as one of the team’s top ICs, taking on the hardest and most critical-path work and unblocking the team members you’re responsible for.

  • Own the architecture. Hold the whole system in your head — services, money-paths, data model, infrastructure, on-chain settlement — and make the design calls that keep it correct, legible, and extensible as it scales.

  • Build the team. Run a rigorous, humane hiring loop; raise the bar; onboard new engineers with real plans; grow a small senior team that works in the open.

  • Set and hold a high engineering bar. Non-author review on money paths, CI required to merge, small PRs, disciplined testing (TDD / BDD as the default, not an afterthought), always-on automated review, idempotency and correctness treated as non-negotiable. Establish safe, effective agentic-development practices as the team's default.

  • Own the delivery cadence. Run a tight, high-velocity delivery process — sprints or kanban, whatever fits the team — with predictable, versioned releases, a healthy backlog, and short lead time from idea to production. Ship fast without lowering the bar.

  • Make it reliable. Drive real production alerting, an on-call rotation that pages a human, tested runbooks, and incident response — so the team can build, ship, and run the product with confidence.

Required Skills and Experience

  • You've led engineering for a consumer money product — a neobank, payments, or crypto money app - where a bug moves or loses real customer money. You owned an engineering function where correctness had genuine financial stakes.

  • You've led a small team (~3–8) while still shipping code yourself — tech lead, staff, or hands-on engineering manager. You've shipped production code within the last year; this is not a management-ladder-only background.

  • You've owned production operations for a money system — on-call, real incidents, observability, secret and key hygiene — not just delegated it. You can name incidents you personally drove to resolution.

  • You've owned, or overseen the integration of, regulated third-party financial rails — at least two of: card issuing / BIN-sponsor programs (Marqeta, Lithic, Kulipa, Stripe Issuing), identity / KYC / onboarding (SumSub, Persona, Onfido), banking or fiat on-/off-ramp partners (a BaaS or ramp partner), and key custody / signing (cloud KMS, HSM, MPC, or multisig).

  • You run a high-velocity, disciplined delivery process. You've led a team that ships fast and predictably in an agile setup — sprints or kanban, versioned releases, short lead time to production — without trading away quality. Test-driven and behaviour-driven development are how you build, not box-ticking.

  • You're agent-native. You wield agentic development — coding agents (e.g. Claude Code), MCP servers, reusable skills — as a core multiplier, with a real point of view on adopting it safely on a money product. Fluent, not a dabbler; you know the failure modes and verify output.

Technical breadth to lead this team

  • You'll lead engineers across backend, platform, and mobile, and set the standard each is built to. You must be deep in backend / distributed systems and genuinely literate across the rest — enough to review the work and make the architecture call in each:

  • Backend & payments correctness (your core). Strong TypeScript / Node (or a credible senior path from Go / Kotlin / Java); you think natively in idempotency, reconciliation, retries, and consistency under partial failure, across event-driven services and Postgres.

  • Client-facing APIs & auth. The app-facing API as a product — versioning, idempotency keys, a clean error model — plus the auth backend behind it (OAuth2 / OIDC, session lifecycle, WebAuthn / passkeys).

  • Platform & reliability. Enough Kubernetes, IaC, and observability (OTel / Grafana-class) to own the deploy/rollback story and hold the reliability bar — you know the difference between a dashboard that exists and an alert that pages.

  • Native mobile. Enough to review a native iOS app (Swift / SwiftUI) and reason about mobile ↔ backend contracts, failure states, and on-device auth.

About the Company

Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

You will have the opportunity to deliver massive impact at a hypergrowth company backed by some of the top investors in fintech, crypto, and SaaS. In January 2026, we closed a $250M Series C led by ICONIQ, valuing Rain at $1.95B, with Sapphire Ventures, Dragonfly, Bessemer Venture Partners, Galaxy Ventures, FirstMark, Lightspeed, Norwest, and Endeavor Catalyst also participating. If you're curious, bold, and excited to help shape a borderless financial future, we'd love to talk.

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About the Team

We're looking for a Technical Support Analyst to help us deliver exceptional support for Rain's platform and integrations. You'll work directly with the fintechs, platforms, and partners building card programs and stablecoin products on Rain — troubleshooting complex API integrations, reading logs, and querying data to resolve issues that touch real money movement at scale. You'll partner closely with almost every team in the company on escalations, and turn what you learn on the ground into fixes that pushes Rain forward.

What you’ll do

  • Investigate and resolve advanced customer and partner issues across Rain's systems, APIs, and integrations.

  • Troubleshoot complex API integrations directly with partners, walking them through clear steps to resolve issues on their end.

  • Own incidents in your queue as part of the team's 24x7 coverage: triage promptly, communicate clearly with clients and internal stakeholders, and consistently hit your SLA, CSAT, and quality targets.

  • Escalate effectively by partnering closely with other teams to get to a satisfactory resolution

  • Maintain accurate documentation and build troubleshooting guides and knowledge base content, supporting both self-serve resolution for customers and onboarding for the team.

  • Feed insights back to Product and Engineering

  • Collaborate with Engineering on testing, monitoring, and alerting improvements, and support new feature rollouts and integrations as they ship.

You are likely to succeed if you have:

  • 3+ years of experience in a technical, customer- or partner-facing support role — ideally in fintech, payments, SaaS, or another high-growth, API-first environment.

  • Hands-on experience with API products, plus comfort reading logs and writing SQL queries to investigate issues

  • Familiarity with support processes and case management best practices

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a detail-oriented, root-cause mindset.

  • Clear writing and communication skills

  • Ability to prioritize effectively and manage multiple complex cases at once

Bonus attributes:

  • A strategic, collaborative, results-oriented approach, and a genuine interest in payments or other areas of fintech.

  • A collaborative mindset, a passion for continuous learning, and a knack for building long-lasting relationships.

  • scripting or lightweight automation experience is a plus.

Things that enable a fulfilling, healthy and happy experience at Rain:

Unlimited time off 🌴 Unlimited vacation can be daunting, so we require Rainmakers to take 10 days minimum for themselves.

Flexible working ☕ We support a flexible workplace – work from home, come into an office, or both. We want everyone to work in an environment where they're their most confident and productive selves. New Rainmakers receive a stipend to set up a comfortable home workspace.

Easy to access benefits 🧠 For US Rainmakers, we cover 95% of your health, dental, and vision plan costs and 90% for your dependents, plus a 100% company-subsidized life insurance plan.

Retirement goals💡 Plan for the future with confidence. We offer a 401(k) with a 4% company match.

Equity plan 📦 Every Rainmaker gets an equity option plan so we all benefit from our success.

Health and Wellness 📚 High performance begins from within. Rainmakers receive a monthly stipend to be used for eligible health and wellness spending like gym memberships/fitness classes, massages, acupuncture - whatever recharges you!

In-office meals 🍜 Rainmakers working from the office enjoy lunch and dinner on us, covered with a DoorDash credit.

Team summits ✨ Summits play an important role at Rain. Time together helps us build relationships and a common destiny. Expect team and company offsites, both domestic and international.

世界で戦う「オンチェーン金融の垂直統合企業」として、チェーン、ステーブルコイン、決済、アプリ——必要なレイヤーのすべてを開発提供しています。SBIグループと共同で、完全オンチェーン版の”東証”といえる取引所「Strium」の構築を進め、国内初の信託型円建てステーブルコイン「JPYSC」を発行済み。ソニーグループとの合弁会社によるエンタメ特化ブロックチェーン「Soneium」と合わせ、これらインフラの入口としてデジタルアセットのスーパーアプリ「Startale App」を提供しています。

文明は、より優れた「価値交換システム」の発明とともに進歩してきました。葉や粘土に取引を刻んだ時代から、紙へ、そしてオンラインへ。次の基盤がオンチェーンです。

お金を払う、資産を取引する——経済活動そのものは変わりません。変わるのは裏側です。いま株式を売買するとき、紙の株券かデータかを気にする人がいないように、将来はそれがトークンかどうかも誰も気にしなくなります。ただ桁違いに速く、安くなり、その上に新しい金融サービスを組み立てられるようになる。米国では株式や債券のトークン化が本格化し、金融機関の問いはすでに「実現するか」から「どう参加するか」に変わりました。

About us:

Luno has spent over a decade making digital assets safe to own. Since 2013, we've helped millions of people across more than 40 countries buy, store and invest in crypto, working with regulators in every market and holding all customer crypto 1:1. That discipline built the licences, banking relationships, custody and compliance machinery that the next era of this market will run on

The financial system is moving on-chain. Stablecoins are the only digital asset class operating at institutional scale today, and while 98% of supply is dollar-pegged, roughly half of global payment flows are not. That gap is the opportunity, and it is largest in exactly the markets Luno has spent twelve years building in.

About the team

You will join the Product Management team building Luno’s institutional business: the activation, digital asset account infrastructure and issuance products that let businesses, institutions and partners operate on Luno’s rails. The portfolio spans Luno Institutional and BlockTower, the group’s stablecoin issuance business. You'll report to the Group Product Manager and work in the BlockTower pod with dedicated engineering and UX partners.

The role in a nutshell:

BlockTower is the group’s institutional stablecoin issuance business, starting with ZARU, the South African rand stablecoin. You'll own the products institutions touch: the self-service issuance platform, where treasury teams mint, redeem, distribute yield and report, and Wallet as a Service, which lets those institutions use and offer stablecoins inside their own  products and flows. Your job is to turn a working product into a repeatable one, and to build the foundation on which future local-currency stablecoins launch in new markets.

Your mission will be:

  • The issuance platform: the portal, mint and redeem flows, yield distribution, user and access management, approval workflows, statements and reporting
  • Wallet as a Service: how institutions embed wallets into their own platforms
  • The boundary: What the platform needs from the underlying Luno infrastructure, and holding the line on what BlockTower owns itself
  • Repeatability: the next currency, chain, market or wallet use case should be a configuration exercise, not a new build 
  • Commercial shape: Take institutional customers live and convert every manual step in their journey into a self-service product
  • Customer-centric: Spend real time with the customers themselves: treasury teams, payment providers, market makers and financial institutions, and let their operating reality shape the roadmap
  • Build the controls institutions require to trust an issuer: auditability, segregation of duties, and reporting that their own compliance teams will accept

A little about you: 

  • You have 3+ years of experience as a Product Manager, including taking a new product from zero to its first paying customers and then through the stage of making it repeatable
  • You have built for institutional users: treasury, payments, capital markets or banking 
  • You deeply understand stablecoins and the economics of issuance: reserves, yield, minting and redemption, and you can reason about how a product decision moves each of them
  • You know your way around on-chain settlement - chains, custody, what moves on-chain versus off, well enough to make clear product trade-offs rather than defer them to engineering
  • You are comfortable operating a young business inside a larger group: small team, broad remit, decisions made with limited information and a parent company whose infrastructure you depend on
  • You work confidently in a regulated environment and can collaborate with legal and compliance on the controls a licensed issuer must carry
  • You are credible in the room with institutional customers, you've been the named person in a treasury team, PSP, market maker or bank calls, and you've turned what those relationships taught you into a roadmap
  • You use AI as part of how you work -in discovery, analysis, writing and prototyping, and you can show where it's changed your output, not just your tooling

Life at Luno:

  • Access to Learnably and our additional learning platforms for your personal and professional development

Numerai is building a self-improving hedge fund.

We run an institutional quant fund built from thousands of machine learning models. Increasingly, those models are built by AI, not people. This isn't a thesis we're pitching. It's already how Numerai gets smarter every day (see https://numer.ai).

The next step is to compound it. Numerai is forming a new team with one mandate: build AI that does quant research autonomously, all the time. Discover new features, build better risk models, improve how the fund turns thousands of signals into a portfolio.

Numerai is a small company with an unusual amount of leverage per person. No bureaucracy, no politics. Significant equity.

The Role

Your job is to expand the set of things Numerai knows how to do: which signals are worth pursuing, which risk structures are worth taking, which ideas look good in backtest and reliably die in production, and where the market is exploitable.

You will develop and evaluate alpha across horizons and data types, from slow fundamental structure to faster cross-sectional effects.

You will work on covariance and factor risk estimation: estimator choice, shrinkage, conditioning, missing and stale data, and the difference between a number that looks stable and a number that is actually right out of sample. You will build the diagnostics that catch a degrading risk model before the portfolio does.

You will work on the optimizer: problem formulation, constraint design, objective specification, numerical conditioning, solver behavior, and the sensitivity of the resulting portfolio to every assumption baked into it. You should be the person who notices that a constraint is quietly doing something nobody intended.

You will help decide what data we buy and what we build, and you'll productionize what works.

You will write up what you find. Research reports, derivations, and clear explanations of why the new formulation is better than the old one. Then you will ship it to production and monitor it.

Requirements

  • PhD in mathematics, statistics, physics, EECS, or a comparably quantitative field — or equivalent demonstrated depth
  • 7+ years in quantitative research, ideally across more than one firm, with strategies that traded real capital and made money
  • Deep working knowledge of factor models, risk decomposition, portfolio optimization, transaction cost modeling, and execution
  • Strong statistical judgment: you have internalized how overfitting actually happens and you design research to avoid fooling yourself
  • Excellent written communication. Your research reports should be able to change someone's mind
  • Comfortable owning work end to end in Python, including the unglamorous parts

Nice to have

  • Global equities and cross-sectional stock selection experience
  • Familiarity with modern portfolio risk and construction literature
  • Experience with numerical linear algebra at scale, or with conic and quadratic solvers
  • Experience with machine learning applied to financial prediction, and a clear sense of where it helps and where it doesn't

Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

We're looking for a CTO who wants to own engineering end to end: the systems, the people, and the standards for a company whose work changes lives.

  • Keep us moving fast as we get bigger: We deliberately favour fewer processes, simple designs, and deeply understood tools, because that's what lets a small team operate a system this important. Your job is to protect that as the headcount grows and ensure more ownership per engineer, and a clear view of where complexity is worth the tradeoff.
  • Own reliability: Wave is the financial system for tens of millions of people. You'll set the standards for uptime, incident response, and how carefully we change things that move money and you'll be accountable when we fall short.
  • Build and lead the leadership layer: You'll inherit 5 direct reports and an engineering organization of ~132 people including security, data and infrastructure. You will be responsible for hiring, developing, and where necessary replacing engineering managers and directors. You'll be personally involved in senior hiring.
  • Set our vision on AI: Set our vision on AI. We’re already seeing AI accelerate product velocity, but we think we’re in the early days of what we can do with AI in our apps and to move faster across the org. We want you to make Wave a truly AI forward organization.
  • Support expansion. Wave already has over 25M users with accelerating growth. This scale and each new market brings new challenges and constraints. You’ll help us plan the right architecture and organizational structure to help us grow smoothly and consistently.
  • Represent engineering to the company. Wave is very transparent, whether that’s defaulting to public conversations in slack, frequent Ask Wave Anything sessions, or defaulting to writing public docs to explain major decisions. You'll communicate openly and clearly about what engineering is doing and why, to an audience that includes engineers, non-engineers, our leadership team, and our when needed regulators.

Key details

Reports to: Drew Durbin, CEO.

Team: Around ~132 engineers across 5 teams (Payment, User-facing products, Internal, non-product teams and platform) plus 5 leaders. Engineering teams are co-led by Product Managers and an engineering manager.

Stack: Python 3 with mypy on the backend, GraphQL API layer, Postgres and Redis, Kotlin/Jetpack on Android (our main client), Swift/SwiftUI on iOS, TypeScript and React on the web. Infrastructure on GCP, managed with Kubernetes and Terraform. Most backend work happens in a large Python monolith, deployed across multi-country architecture. Current in-flight work includes agentic developer tooling, a large scale migration of our databases, and some refactoring of our monolith. 

Location: This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (Spain, UK, East Coast of USA, Canada, Kenya, Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso etc. Expect to travel to our markets a minimum of twice per year to stay close to local realities, products, teams and of course our users. Wave covers all costs.

Compensation: Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary of up to $356,500 USD, plus a generous equity package:

  • Wave provides a yearly $1,200 stipend to support coworking meetups with teammates.
  • Major benefits:
    • Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country).
    • 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance.
    • Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days exclusive of statutory holidays.
    • $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

Process: The process runs up to 5 conversations, including 2 technical discussions. We want this to be a 2-way assessment: as much a chance for you to evaluate us as for us to get to know you. Along the way you'll meet our CEO, Head of People, Head of Product, both Engineering Directors, and a senior leader from one of our markets.

Requirements

  • You've managed an engineering organization of at ~100 people, including managers who manage others. You can describe how your own job changed as the org grew.
  • You have a software engineering background and are good at it. You can still read code and follow a technical argument to the end.
  • You've been accountable for a system where failure was expensive: money, safety, or regulated data.
  • You've hired senior engineering leaders, and you've moved someone out of a role that wasn't working. You can talk about both honestly.
  • You write well. Clear, short, and persuasive, for readers who aren't engineers.
  • You have a clear and positive point of view on AI in engineering: something you've tried, changed, or abandoned, not a plan to look into it.
  • You believe in what we're building and can say why without being prompted.

You might be a good fit if you

  • Would rather run a great team than be the smartest engineer in the room, and don't feel a loss in that trade.
  • Are comfortable being the person who says the unwelcome thing in a meeting, and can do it without making it personal.
  • Change your mind in public when the evidence changes.
  • Prefer the simplest system that works to the most interesting one.
  • Care about what our users actually experience: how long a transfer takes on a bad network, what happens to a shop owner when a deposit fails and bring that up unprompted when discussing infrastructure.
  • Take responsibility for outcomes rather than processes, including when the outcome is bad.
  • Are drawn to a company that publishes its numbers internally every month, expects direct feedback in both directions, and would rather be embarrassingly honest than comfortable.

Our team

  • We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.
  • We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.
  • We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.
  • We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.
  • We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue.

How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Mesh is looking for an exceptional leader to build and scale our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) organization — a new function at the company, starting with you. We have a strong preference for someone who resides in the New York City area or San Francisco. 

Reporting to our CTO, you'll lead a team of senior engineers who embed directly with a small, capped set of our most strategic partners — exchanges, neobanks, and prediction markets that drive the lion's share of our volume. These partners aren't buying a static product off the shelf. They're buying working crypto rails inside their product, against their brokers, their compliance posture, and their release schedule. The gap between a demo that works and a production integration that survives contact with a partner's environment is where deals stall, and where generic support queues and quarterly roadmap cycles fail.

Our thesis is simple: FDE sits inside Engineering, not in a services org. An FDE ships code that lands in the account and when it generalizes in our core platform. Engagements are time-boxed with a clear "ship something working end-to-end" milestone — not open-ended residencies. And the function stays deliberately small. The moment it needs a manager of managers, it has stopped being FDE and become consulting with an engineering badge. Holding that line is a core part of the job.

This role requires equal parts technical judgment, commercial acumen, and organizational leadership. You need to be technical enough to earn immediate credibility with a partner's top engineers, scope an integration live on a call, and call out a bad architectural decision — but your leverage comes from the team you build and the alignment you drive, not from the code you personally write.

What You'll Do

Build and scale the FDE organization

  • Define the operating model: engagement shape, deployment cadence, scoping standards, and hiring bar
  • Hire at least 2-3 senior and staff-level generalists this year placed close to the partner engineering team and timezone they support
  • Be open to running the first engagement(s) yourself to prove the playbook, then scale it through the team

Own delivery at our most strategic accounts

  • Be the person a partner's VP of Engineering or CTO calls — run integration reviews, hold commitments, and turn stalled technical conversations into signed plans
  • Assign named owners, not a rotating pool: one engineer or small pod per account, with a mapped executive sponsor
  • Own the qualification bar. FDE is justified when integration is the bottleneck, the account can absorb a dedicated engineer, speed decides the deal, or the pattern generalizes to the next ten partners
  • Set the boundary with Customer Success, who own the relationship, and Support, who own break-fix. CS flags what an account needs; you decide whether it's an FDE build, a platform ask, or neither
  • Measure partner growth, volume, and time-to-production — not tickets closed

Shape product and platform strategy

  • Turn the sharpest signal in the company — what partners need in production — into scoped, prioritized platform input
  • Enforce the productization ratchet: what's built either generalizes into our shared platform inside a defined window, or we stop re-investing in it. Guard against both failure modes — a silent per-customer fork, and a core roadmap hijacked by one-off asks
  • Build reference architectures, QA, and monitoring that catch failure modes inside the integration rather than in a support queue

Who You Are

Leadership and team building

  • 10+ years in technical roles, with 4+ years leading forward-deployed teams
  • Experience building a 0→1 organization or a new service line inside an existing company
  • A track record of attracting, developing, and retaining senior engineers in a competitive market, including personally closing candidates

Technical credibility

  • You came up as a strong backend or integrations engineer and can still read a codebase, whiteboard a system, debug a design, and review architecture alongside your team. You are not expected to be in the codebase day to day
  • Substantial experience with broker, exchange, or payments integration patterns and crypto rails. Our partners' engineers will spot someone learning the domain on the job in the first meeting
  • A history of embedding with customer engineering teams to deliver complex technical work in production

Commercial and strategic acumen

  • Strong executive presence — effective and composed in front of partner executives and our own leadership team, including when an integration is on fire
  • Client-facing instincts: you like being in front of partners, can read a room, and can separate the stated ask from the real constraint
  • Willingness to push back. You've declined bad requests from partners and internal stakeholders alike, and driven alignment across engineering, revenue, and product without escalating every disagreement
  • Experience defining engagement models, scoping, and pricing for technical delivery work

The annual base salary range for this role is $282,000 - $355,000, plus equity, in New York or San Francisco. The compensation range provided may span multiple career levels and will be narrowed during the interview process based on factors including a candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location. For candidates outside of New York or San Francisco, compensation will be adjusted to reflect the applicable market and location-based pay band. The base salary range listed excludes commission (if applicable), equity, and benefits. The pay range represents the minimum and maximum target for new-hire compensation. Actual compensation may vary and may be higher or lower depending on individual circumstances.

Why You’ll Love It Here

At Mesh, you're not stepping into a typical role—you're joining a rocket ship in mid-liftoff. You'll tackle complex, meaningful problems that actually move an industry forward, working alongside a sharp, motivated team that moves quickly, collaborates deeply, and expects everyone to operate with ownership. This is the kind of place where you'll see your work ship fast, make real impact, and be able to point to something and say, "I built that." You'll grow fast, level up your skills, and get a front-row seat to how a high-growth company scales from the inside, with competitive comp, solid benefits, and room to stretch your craft all coming standard. If you're energized by building, learning, and shaping something big—this is where you'll want to be.

In-Office Expectations

Employees based in our San Francisco, New York, and Bangalore hubs are expected to work from the office at least 40% of the time (approximately two days per week). This expectation may vary slightly depending on role, team, and business needs. Certain roles that require closer cross-functional collaboration or operational support may have additional in-office requirements, which will be discussed during the interview process. Our hybrid approach is designed to balance meaningful in-person collaboration, team building, and real-time decision-making with the flexibility to work remotely. We believe this structure supports strong execution while preserving autonomy and focus time.

How We Care For Our Team

We believe great work happens when people feel valued and supported. That starts with competitive salary and equity that grows as you and the company grow, plus comprehensive health coverage for you and your family. We offer unlimited PTO—and we mean it. Take the time you need to recharge and show up at your best.

We're invested in your growth with a dedicated budget for courses, conferences, and certifications. Work from wherever you're most productive with our remote-friendly approach, and count on having the top-tier tools and equipment you need to do exceptional work.

Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Our Regulatory Legal team is the group responsible for maintaining and growing Kraken’s product offerings across the EU and UK and for advising the business on its day-to-day regulatory obligations. We’re a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech, and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious, and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice – partnering directly with Compliance, Product, and senior leadership to keep our licensed entities running smoothly and our regulators well served.

The Senior Counsel role is a remote role based in the UK or the EU, and will report into the EU/UK Regulatory Legal team. The role exists to own the significant volume of ongoing, business-as-usual regulatory work that currently falls to a small group of very senior lawyers – freeing them to focus on strategic licensing initiatives, complex transactions, and team leadership.

You will operate as a practical legal generalist with focus on:

  • Product advice covering Payward’s growing offerings in the EU and UK (Krak card, payments and staking, among other things)

  • Cryptoasset Regime Compliance (under MiCA/EU or in the UK) — advising on regulatory obligations for CASPs including supporting on the steady flow of regulatory queries, notifications and supervisory correspondence that keeps our licensed entities compliant and our regulatory relationships strong; and

  • Payments & e-money compliance — advising on regulatory obligations affecting our e-money and payment accounts and supporting related workstreams as they arise.

We’re looking for a hands-on lawyer with strong regulatory fluency and a track record of independently owning BAU regulatory relationships (ideally honed in the regulated financial sector).

This is a fully remote role for a qualified lawyer in the UK or EU.

 

The opportunity

  • Provide legal support on cryptoasset, e-money and payment services regulatory requirements, including advising on account-access obligations and related operational compliance questions

  • Support the team’s active licensing applications and other in-flight EU/UK licensing or registration workstreams, including compiling application materials and coordinating with outside counsel

  • Provide regulatory support on corporate transactions and structural changes affecting EU/UK entities (e.g., change-of-control notifications, corporate client migrations)

  • Support the day-to-day relationship with regulators for our licensed entities

  • Translate complex regulatory frameworks (e.g., MiCA and the UK Cryptoasset Regime, CBI and FCA rulebooks, AML/CTF, DORA, outsourcing requirements, and e-money and payment services regulation) into pragmatic, actionable guidance for the business

  • Foster a culture of clarity, favouring plain-English communication, measurable risk tradeoffs, and decision-ready recommendations

 

What you bring

  • Qualified lawyer (Solicitor/Barrister of England & Wales, Irish Solicitor/Barrister, or equivalent admitted in an EU Member State)

  • 10+ years’ post-qualification experience (PQE) in financial services regulatory law gained at a regulated financial services institution (e.g., a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, or crypto services provider) or in a law firm/private practice supporting such clients, with demonstrated ability to independently own BAU regulatory workstreams

  • Direct experience supporting regulator engagement (e.g., with the CBI, FCA, or an equivalent EU competent authority), including notifications, information requests, and supervisory correspondence

  • Substantive experience advising on MiCA or the UK Cryptoasset Regime (i.e., FCA authorisation for regulated cryptoasset activities under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026) — experience with one regime is sufficient; both is not required

  • Substantive experience with e-money and payment services regulation in the EU or UK (experience in one jurisdiction is sufficient; both is not required), including account-access and open banking obligations

  • Experience in AML/CTF (anti-money laundering / counter-terrorist financing), including advising on related policies, controls, and regulatory expectations

  • Experience advising on outsourcing arrangements and operational resilience compliance (e.g., Digital Operational Resilience Act in the EU, or the FCA/PRA operational resilience regime in the UK)

  • Outstanding analytical, drafting, and organisational skills with crisp, plain-English writing

  • Ability to efficiently and confidently distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders

  • Pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that prioritises providing stakeholders with a useful range of options and clear recommendations

  • Comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy and owning a broad, fast-moving BAU workload from day one

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Familiarity with MiFID II and its application to investment services, including derivatives, equities, and emerging tokenised financial instruments

  • Experience supporting change-of-control notifications or other regulatory aspects of corporate transactions

  • An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward’s and competitors’ products

About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, PayPal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We're backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NfX and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

OpenFX processes billions of dollars in transaction volume every month across global corridors. The Growth pod owns everything a client touches before and while they become a paying, trading customer: the public API they integrate against, the onboarding and verification journey that gets them approved, the activation surface that gets them to their first trade, and the marketing site that brings them in.

Client onboarding runs today on third-party tooling and is being brought in-house, which means rebuilding KYB and KYC as our own product rather than a vendor workflow. And onboarding policy is still effectively global, when the business needs requirements that vary by jurisdiction and customer segment.

Every point of friction across those surfaces is a client who does not activate, or who activates slowly and expensively. The work is also unusually dependency-heavy: nearly every onboarding item depends on Compliance and Legal, the API programme depends on Platform, Payments, Banking, and Client Trading, and the website work depends on Brand Design.

We need an Engineering Manager who can hold four surfaces at once, ship inside a stage-gated product process without letting it become theatre, and keep a correctness bar on flows that touch identity, compliance, and the money path.

If we do not solve this well, activation stays gated on manual work and vendor tooling, and growth stays bottlenecked on ad hoc engineering requests.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run the Growth pod of roughly 6 to 10 engineers and QA across frontend, backend, and integrations. You own the roadmap, the delivery, and the standards.
  • Own the API as a product. Land the V3 overhaul, our largest and most cross-dependent programme, while V2 stays supported. Ship client-facing API.
  • Bring onboarding in-house. Move the client onboarding experience off third-party tools onto OpenFX, and build the rules engine that replaces global policy with dynamic KYB and KYC requirements by jurisdiction and customer segment.
  • Extend onboarding to new segments — self-serve signup through to first trade with no sales touch, enterprise (large entities, directors, UBO, bespoke verification), channel partners and platform-of-platforms, multi-product onboarding across banking and payments, and eventually agent-based customers.
  • Own the activation surface: digital signatures, in-product activation checklists, recovery and lifecycle client comms, and a self-serve notification centre.
  • Own the marketing site as a growth surface, partnering with Brand Design and the visual explainers that both generate market intelligence and give sales what they need to close.
  • Run the product development process credibly. Take work from discovery through solution, design, and RFC validation into delivery and beta, own or assign RFCs, and hold the design-ready and delivery-ready gates so nothing enters a sprint half-shaped.
  • Manage a dependency-saturated roadmap. Compliance, Legal, Platform, Payments, Banking, Currencies, TPV, Client Trading, Brand Design, and GTM all sit on your critical path. Sequencing around them is a core part of the job, not an interruption to it.
  • Own the interface with GTM and Product: one intake for growth and sales requests, joint prioritisation with the Growth PM, and an expedite lane whose cost in displaced work is explicit rather than silently absorbed.
  • Stay hands-on. You review designs, and you still write and ship code, debug production, and set the implementation bar by example, including the standard for AI-assisted development.
  • Hold the bar where correctness is not optional: identity and KYC deduplication, idempotency on quote and trade paths, permission and compliance boundaries, money precision and rounding.
  • Hire and grow the team: close open roles, grow your team, run 30-60-90 ramps, set explicit performance expectations, and act on them early.

What We Are Looking For

Must-haves:

  • EM-level scope: 2 or more years managing a full team of 5 or more, with a Tech Lead or senior IC reporting in, on top of a strong individual contributor track record.
  • Still writes code. You can design an API, model a schema, and produce idiomatic, runnable, tested code. Design fluency without hands-on ability is not enough at this level.
  • Experience owning a public or partner-facing API as a product, including versioning and running an old and a new major version side by side.
  • Shipped client-facing product end to end, including the unglamorous parts: migrations, deprecations, and error states.
  • Has delivered against Compliance and Legal as hard dependencies, not as a review step at the end. Onboarding at OpenFX is a compliance surface first and a product surface second.
  • Comfortable running a stage-gated product process — discovery, solution and design validation, RFC, delivery — without letting it slow the team down or become box-ticking.
  • Can take a one-line placeholder and turn it into shaped, sized, sequenced work. A large share of the forward roadmap is deliberately undefined.
  • Demonstrated hiring and performance management, including at least one underperformance case you saw through to an outcome.
  • Has worked directly with Product and a commercial or GTM function, and can say no with a reason that holds.
  • High agency: operates with low oversight on ambiguous problems, in a demanding environment.
  • Can articulate and enforce a correctness bar under commercial time pressure.

What helps you stand out:

  • Fintech, payments, or another regulated domain where onboarding is a compliance surface.
  • KYB and KYC in production, and replacing a vendor onboarding or verification workflow with an in-house build.
  • Jurisdiction-aware or segment-aware policy engines, where requirements are configuration rather than code branches.
  • Developer experience work: API documentation, SDKs, sandbox environments, webhook delivery, or developer funnels.
  • Activation and lifecycle engineering: in-product onboarding checklists, transactional and lifecycle comms, notification preferences.
  • Marketing site or growth-experiment engineering in partnership with Brand Design.
  • Growth instrumentation and analytics tooling, and comfort reading a funnel yourself.
  • Onboarding for enterprise entities (directors, UBO) or for channel partners and platform-of-platforms models.

What Success Looks Like

  • Share of TPV through the API, with a target of 60%. The V3 overhaul, webhook reliability, and API observability are the levers.
  • Activated customers, with a target of 200+. Onboarding, digital signatures, and the activation surface are the levers.
  • Annualised TPV, contributing to an annualised $250B dollar goal.
  • Zero lights-out compliance and financial crime findings on the flows you own.
  • Predictable delivery: commitments land on the dates given, and when they slip you flag it early with a revised plan rather than late with an explanation.
  • Dependencies land: work with Compliance, Legal, Platform, and Brand Design closes on schedule because you drove it, not because it happened to unblock.
  • Discovery converts: ambiguous placeholder initiatives become shaped, sized, RFC-validated work rather than sitting at low confidence for a quarter.
  • Quality on the identity and money path: onboarding and API defects are caught by tests and monitoring, not by clients.
  • Team strength: fully staffed and ramped, your Tech Lead is growing, strong performers stay, and weak performance is addressed rather than tolerated.
  • Talent magnetism: you bring strong engineers with you and raise the bar of every loop you sit on.

Why This Role

  • Impact: You own the surfaces that decide whether a client activates and whether their volume comes through our API. Both are company-level KPIs.
  • Ownership: The pod, the roadmap, the quality bar, and the GTM interface are all yours to set.
  • Scope: Four surfaces, not one: public API, onboarding and verification, activation, and the marketing site. Few EM roles span that much of the customer journey.
  • Build, not maintain: Onboarding is coming off vendor tooling, the API is being overhauled, and much of the Q4 roadmap is still undefined. You are shaping it, not inheriting it.
  • Learning: Cross-border payments, FX, and settlement, with compliance and correctness constraints that make the problems genuinely hard.
  • Access: Direct partnership with the Growth PM, the Head of GTM, Compliance and Legal leadership, and senior engineering leadership.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Equity in a rapidly growing company.
  • Opportunity to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation.
  • Opportunity to make a significant impact on global financial infrastructure.
  • Collaborative work culture with emphasis on personal and professional growth.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

We're building the company which will de-risk the largest infrastructure build-out in history.

When people finance GPU clusters, the datacenters housing them, and the infrastructure powering them, they need "offtake" - meaning someone has signed a contract to lease the cluster for a period of time before its even built.

Financing a GPU cluster is inherently risky, since margins are thin and volumes are huge. Lenders don't want to take on the risk that cluster developers can't repay their loan, and cluster developers really don't want to risk not selling their cluster. As a result, risk is offloaded to the customer using fixed-price long-term contracts.

If you don't mitigate this customer risk, there's a bubble. This isn't SaaS anymore - application layer companies sign multi-year contracts for computer and inference, but sell to customers on monthly subscriptions. If you mess up a purchase, it's game over: a minor shift in your revenue growth rate might mean the difference between profit or bankruptcy. But what if companies could exit their contract by selling it back to the market?

Otherwise, as AI scales, compute only becomes available to folks who can effectively take on that risk. A 2-person startup in a San Francisco Victorian can't realistically sign a 5-year take or pay contract on $100m supercomputers. But they may be able to buy the month of liquidity that someone else sold back.

So that's what we make: a liquid market for GPU offtake.

We're building the company which will de-risk the largest infrastructure build-out in history.

When people finance GPU clusters, the datacenters housing them, and the infrastructure powering them, they need "offtake" - meaning someone has signed a contract to lease the cluster for a period of time before its even built.

Financing a GPU cluster is inherently risky, since margins are thin and volumes are huge. Lenders don't want to take on the risk that cluster developers can't repay their loan, and cluster developers really don't want to risk not selling their cluster. As a result, risk is offloaded to the customer using fixed-price long-term contracts.

If you don't mitigate this customer risk, there's a bubble. This isn't SaaS anymore - application layer companies sign multi-year contracts for computer and inference, but sell to customers on monthly subscriptions. If you mess up a purchase, it's game over: a minor shift in your revenue growth rate might mean the difference between profit or bankruptcy. But what if companies could exit their contract by selling it back to the market?

Otherwise, as AI scales, compute only becomes available to folks who can effectively take on that risk. A 2-person startup in a San Francisco Victorian can't realistically sign a 5-year take or pay contract on $100m supercomputers. But they may be able to buy the month of liquidity that someone else sold back.

So that's what we make: a liquid market for GPU offtake.

About the role

This is a role for a legal strategist–not a gatekeeper. We're building novel financial infrastructure in a market that doesn't have a rulebook yet. Our General Counsel must be a first-class business partner in the room where deals get shaped, not a checkpoint they pass through at the end.
