About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like PayPal Ventures, Paradigm, and Galaxy Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview

Mesh is seeking our first Head of Card Product.

Crypto solved receiving value. It has not solved spending it. Hundreds of millions of people hold crypto they cannot use to buy fuel or groceries. Every previous fix asked the merchant to change... new software, new assets, new risk... and merchants declined. The result is a vicious cycle: because crypto is not spendable, consumers do not hold much of it. Because consumers do not hold much of it, merchants do not accept it.

We are breaking the cycle from the other side. A user pays with crypto. The merchant receives an ordinary card payment. Nothing changes at the point of sale, so everything changes for the consumer: crypto becomes spendable at over a hundred million merchants in more than two hundred countries overnight... including the markets where people are already paid in stablecoins and have nowhere to spend them. It stops being an asset you hold and becomes money you use.

You will own this program end-to-end: the consumer experience, the bank partnership, the network relationship, and the compliance framework that makes it real. Card programs are not won with code. They are won by earning the confidence of banks and networks, which is why so few companies can build this. If you have spent your career learning how card programs really work, this is the seat where that knowledge changes what money can do.

What You'll Do

  • Own the card program end to end. You are the single accountable owner of this product ... its launch, its growth, its economics. If it touches the program, it's yours.
  • Earn the confidence of banks and networks. You will sit across from bank officers, network compliance teams, and regulators ... in every market the program touches ... and get to yes on KYC, fraud, refunds, and every edge case of how money moves. You write the specificity a bank signs. This is hands-on work, not delegated work.
  • Make paying with crypto feel effortless. Provisioning a card into a wallet, confirming on device, recovering from a failed or disputed transaction. You decide what the user believes is happening and make every screen and state consistent with that belief.
  • Win distribution through wallet partners. This product only matters if wallets carry it. You pitch it, shape each integration, and make partners successful ... their volume is the scoreboard.
  • Decide what cards become at Mesh. Today it is one program. New programs, networks, geographies, and commercialization are yours to figure out ... and to argue for at the exec table with evidence.

Who You Are

  • Experience: You have owned a regulated financial product that shipped through a bank partner or regulator ... a card program, a lending product, a banking or money movement product. Card program experience is a strong plus, not a requirement.
  • Compliance Fluency: You have earned a compliance sign-off from a bank partner, network, or regulator ... KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, fraud, disputes. You can describe a decision a bank pushed back on and how you got to yes.  Experience across multiple markets or regulatory regimes is a strong plus.
  • Consumer Product Judgment: You have owned a consumer payments or fintech product and its outcome ... volume, activation, retention, or P&L. You can walk through a flow you shipped and the reasoning behind it.
  • Mobile Payments: You have shipped device-level payment experiences ... secure element or secure enclave integration, push provisioning, token requestor work with the networks. 
  • AI Leverage: You use AI daily to draft program documentation, model economics, and automate the operational work of running a program.
  • Crypto: Ideally, you have built products that integrate into crypto wallets like MetaMask, Trust Wallet, or Phantom.

Then go further ... rewards, just-in-time lending, and more.

Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

  • Manage, build, and mentor a high-performing team to execute on key initiatives and achieve business goals.

  • The position is based in Niamey.
  • You must have work authorization in Niger.
  • This is a permanent position.
  • Our salaries are competitive and calculated using a transparent formula. We run performance reviews twice a year and award bonuses to strong performers who have been with the company for more than 6 months.

  • We support working parents - we offer parental leave policies (26 weeks for mothers and 4 weeks for fathers) and subsidized childcare when you return to work.

  • Free food and a beautiful office space.

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Velocity is revolutionising the global financial landscape by unifying fiat and digital assets through regulated stablecoin technology. We are tackling some of the most significant inefficiencies in global payments, from the limitations of SWIFT to the cost and delays of cross-border transactions.

Founded by Eric Queathem, with decades of experience scaling and leading payments businesses, Velocity combines deep expertise in regulated financial systems with a fast-growing team across London, Warsaw, New York and Melbourne.

Our platform enables businesses to manage payments, treasury functions, and liquidity in real time, operating 24/7/365. We remove friction in global payouts, cross-border settlements, and treasury operations, seamlessly integrating stablecoin-powered speed with the reliability of traditional finance.

Backed by robust partnerships, including strategic collaborations with Fireblocks and other leading technology providers, we are building trusted infrastructure for scalable global growth.

We recently announced a $38m Series A led by Dragonfly and FirstMark, with participation from QED, Capital One Ventures, Ripple and Coinbase Ventures.

The role

This is a senior, quota-carrying role leading Velocity's sales efforts into the largest and most complex fintech and payments companies across EMEA, working alongside a growing commercial team in London.

You will sell regulated stablecoin payment infrastructure into financial institutions, issuers, acquirers, large PSPs, global marketplaces, and scaled fintechs. Deals are multi-threaded, multi-quarter, and involve treasury, payments, product, risk, and compliance stakeholders on the other side of the table.

Beyond your own number, you will raise the ceiling on how we sell: taking on the accounts that need the most seniority in the room, sharpening pricing and positioning for complex enterprise deals, and working with Velocity's leadership team to shape commercial strategy and prioritisation across the region.

Key responsibilities

  • Own a revenue quota against a portfolio of strategic and enterprise accounts, and be accountable for pipeline generation, progression, and closed business.

  • Source and build your own pipeline through outbound, network, events, and inbound follow-up, with the seniority to open doors at CFO, Treasurer, and Head of Payments level.

  • Own the full sales cycle end to end: prospecting, pitching, discovery, solution shaping, commercial and legal negotiation, close, and go-live, typically spanning several quarters and multiple decision-makers.

  • Structure and negotiate commercially significant agreements, including pricing, liquidity, and settlement terms, in partnership with Finance and Legal.

  • Drive adoption of Velocity across the EMEA payments ecosystem, and build a repeatable, disciplined sales motion with clear qualification, pipeline management, and forecasting.

  • Act as a force multiplier for the wider commercial team, setting the standard on deal strategy and supporting more junior sellers on complex opportunities.

  • Work closely with Product to translate enterprise requirements into product direction, and carry the weight to influence roadmap prioritisation.

  • Represent Velocity at senior level at industry conferences and events across the region.

What we are looking for

  • 6-10+ years' experience in enterprise sales, business development, or partnerships, the majority of it in a quota-carrying closing role.

  • Deep payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure experience, with a sophisticated understanding of how money moves cross-border and where cost, float, and friction sit.

  • A demonstrable track record of consistently hitting or exceeding quota on complex enterprise deals, and the numbers to back it up.

  • Experience closing large, multi-stakeholder deals with financial institutions, PSPs, acquirers, marketplaces, or scaled fintechs, including navigating procurement, risk, and compliance review.

  • A strong, established network across the EMEA payments or fintech ecosystem that you can activate from day one.

  • Experience selling technical or API-based products to business and institutional buyers, with the credibility to hold a conversation with both a treasurer and an engineer.

  • Exposure to stablecoins or digital assets is an advantage, but deep payments experience matters more than prior crypto experience.

Nice to have

Deep experience in one or more of the verticals we sell into:

  • Issuing: issuer-processors, BIN sponsors, and card programme managers, and the funding and settlement mechanics that sit behind a card programme.

  • Acquiring: merchant acquirers, payment facilitators, and ISOs, and where scheme settlement timing, prefunding, and merchant payout cycles tie up working capital.

  • Cross-border and remittance: money transfer operators and remittance providers, correspondent banking relationships, and the cost of holding pre-funded balances across corridors.

  • Banks and EMIs: treasury, liquidity, and nostro management inside a regulated balance sheet.

Why join?

  1. Work on a groundbreaking, forward-thinking solution: Be part of a team leveraging cutting-edge technologies to transform the global financial landscape.

  2. Mission-driven environment with purpose: At Velocity, we prioritize security and user empowerment, ensuring our solutions are built with integrity and designed to make a difference.

  3. Learn from industry leaders: The founding team consists of seasoned operators with a proven track record in the industry, providing invaluable mentorship and guidance as we grow.

  4. Backed by top-tier venture capital: Velocity is supported by premier investors, providing the resources and backing necessary to scale rapidly and execute on our ambitious vision.

  5. Shape the future of global finance: Join an innovative team working on a revolutionary solution that is changing the long-term trajectory of financial operations.

  6. Be part of a company with long-term vision: With a strong regulatory-first approach and a focus on sustainable, scalable growth, Velocity is poised for long-term success.

Benefits

  • Shared ownership: Everyone owns a share of the company. One of our values is to act like an owner, and we back that up with real ownership in the business.

  • Equipment: It is important to have the best tools for the job. We will provide you with a MacBook and will update them regularly. We use all the best modern tools, and if you find an even more efficient way of doing something, we'll adopt it.

  • Health and wellbeing: Paid sick leave, plus medical cover.

  • Pension Contribution

  • Time off: 25 days' holiday plus UK bank holidays.

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like PayPal Ventures, Paradigm, and Galaxy Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview 

We are hiring a Senior Regulatory Counsel to help lead the legal side of Mesh’s global expansion. Working with the Chief Legal Officer and VP of Legal, you will own global regulatory strategy and market entry across LATAM, the EU, the UK, and APAC: assessing what it takes to launch in each market, shaping how our products are offered and distributed there, and driving the licensing and authorization workstreams that make it possible. You will work hand in hand with Compliance, Product, Sales, and outside counsel, and turn a complex, multi-jurisdiction picture into a clear, sequenced expansion plan. This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable operating across borders, legal systems, and time zones at startup speed.

What You'll Do

  • Own global regulatory strategy and market-entry planning across LATAM, the EU, the UK, and APAC, including licensing and authorization requirements, sequencing, and go/no-go recommendations.
  • Lead the regulatory workstreams for priority expansions: the Brazil VASP/SPSAV authorization (and any related acquisition), UK FCA registration and the FSMA authorisation regime, EU frameworks (MiCAR, EMI, and PSD2), and Singapore/MAS.
  • Structure global product and distribution: how features are localized, offered, and distributed in each market, and the partner, reseller, and agent structures that support them.
  • Partner with Compliance and regional MLROs on licensing applications, regulator engagement, and change-of-control and controller approvals.
  • Select, manage, and coordinate outside counsel across jurisdictions, setting scope, budget, and timelines and synthesizing their advice into decisions.
  • Structure and stand up local entities for new markets, including cross-border entity setup and corporate structuring.
  • Advise the business on market-entry risk and sequencing, translating multi-jurisdiction requirements into clear, practical guidance.
  • Monitor regulatory and policy developments across target markets and adjust the expansion roadmap accordingly.

Who You Are

  • 8+ years of relevant legal experience, with significant time spent on cross-border or international financial services, payments, or crypto/digital-asset regulation
  • Deep knowledge of financial services, payments, and crypto regulatory regimes in key markets (LATAM, UK, EU, APAC)
  • Track record leading market-entry, licensing, registration, and authorization projects across multiple jurisdictions
  • Experience structuring and standing up entities, including cross-border entity formation and corporate structuring
  • Practical, risk-based judgment, with comfort operating across borders, legal systems, and time zones at startup speed
  • Strong cross-functional collaborator with Compliance, Product, and Sales, with the judgment to know what to decide versus escalate
  • JD and active membership in good standing with at least one US state bar, or an equivalent qualification in a relevant jurisdiction

The compensation range provided may span multiple career levels and will be narrowed during the interview process based on factors including a candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location. For candidates outside of New York or San Francisco, compensation will be adjusted to reflect the applicable market and location-based pay band. Actual compensation may vary and may be higher or lower depending on individual circumstances.

Pay Range
$250,000—$280,000 USD

Why You’ll Love It Here

At Mesh, you're not stepping into a typical role—you're joining a rocket ship in mid-liftoff. You'll tackle complex, meaningful problems that actually move an industry forward, working alongside a sharp, motivated team that moves quickly, collaborates deeply, and expects everyone to operate with ownership. This is the kind of place where you'll see your work ship fast, make real impact, and be able to point to something and say, "I built that." You'll grow fast, level up your skills, and get a front-row seat to how a high-growth company scales from the inside, with competitive comp, solid benefits, and room to stretch your craft all coming standard. If you're energized by building, learning, and shaping something big—this is where you'll want to be.

We believe this structure supports strong execution while preserving autonomy and focus time.

How We Care For Our Team

We believe great work happens when people feel valued and supported. About Figure

Figure (NASDAQ: FIGR) is transforming capital markets through blockchain. We’re proving that blockchain isn’t just theory - it’s powering real products used by hundreds of thousands of consumers and institutions. 

By combining blockchain’s transparency and efficiency with AI-driven automation, we’ve reimagined how loans are originated, funded, and traded in secondary markets. From faster processing times to lower costs and reduced bias, our technology is helping borrowers, investors, and financial institutions achieve better outcomes.

Together with our 170+ partners, we’ve originated over $22 billion in home equity loans (HELOCs) on our blockchain-native platform, making Figure the largest non-bank provider of home equity financing in the U.S. Figure’s ecosystem also includes YLDS, an SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin that operates as a tokenized money market fund, and several other products and platforms that are reshaping consumer finance and capital markets. 

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Most Innovative Fintech Startups in 2025 and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies in Finance and Personal Finance.

About the Role

Figure is looking for an experienced backend Mortgage/HELOC originating professional to join our Operations team. In this role you will own the Figure HELOC post close process from beginning to end, leveraging your experience and expertise of the role to ensure we have recordable security instruments . The Post Close Operations Associate will manage all investor inquiries related to recorded deed of trust, note, assignments of mortgage, managing/shipping of trailing documents, as well as processing and recording of Assignments of Mortgage. Join this innovative team and make a big impact!

What You’ll Do

  • Partner with customer operations and processing to ensure a smooth post close mortgage process
  • Provide exceptional customer service to both internal and external customers
  • Be process focused and continuously look for opportunities for improvements and efficiencies
  • Work independently to prioritize work based on investor delivery expiration and closing dates
  • Handle tasks such as printing, signing, notarizing, and recording relevant documents
  • Process paper Assignments of Mortgage (AOMs) related to loan sales and securitizations
  • Manage the Power of Attorney (POA) and AOM process for Private Label Partners until 100% of volume is on DART
  • Oversee the onboarding and offboarding of DART loans via AOMs, ensuring timely and accurate processing
  • Manage the processing of new PLDs, document revisions, and handling of tax affidavits, FP7, and other necessary paperwork in collaboration with our vendors.
  • Address security instrument exceptions and lien release issues, including conducting county research, outreach, and resolving recording exceptions.
  • Manage RSD tasks when closing defects are identified, dispositioning appropriately for next steps.
  • Manage outreach efforts for unsecured liens, including calls, emails, FedEx letters, and SandCastle orders. 
  • Process documents for closing  appointments as necessary
  • Handle curative efforts such as Scrivener's Affidavits and other document corrections, ensuring all documentation is accurate and compliant.
  • Monitor the recording stage audit and ensure accountability for all security instruments (SIs), working with vendors to resolve outstanding liens and secure recorded SIs.

NYC, Full-Time, In-Person

The Situation

Honcho is ripping. 50x developer growth in three months. 40,000 prosumers and developers. 600+ startups applied to our startup program in eight weeks.

We're a product-coupled neolab solving personal identity for the agentic world. The market currently calls what we do memory, but the vision for Honcho is much more ambitious. We build better models of you than you have of yourself. The goal is true 1:1 individual alignment for every human extending their cognition and agency with artificial intelligence.

That vision has an infrastructure bill attached. A model of every individual user, updated continuously, queryable in the loop of someone else's agent, is a genuinely hard systems problem--stateful, write-heavy, and unforgiving at scale. Growth like ours makes every architectural decision load-bearing, and we're making those decisions now.

The repo has its own gravity, too. Honcho is open source, and we maintain integrations with Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, and more arriving faster than we can staff them. The agent ecosystem is moving quickly enough that this is a permanent condition, not a backlog we clear.

We need more talented people who can hold the whole thing in their head.

The Job

You'll work directly with the CTO to architect and maintain Honcho: continual learning infrastructure for AI memory and identity modeling.

Own the core. The systems that store, update, and serve per-user models are yours. Not a service you contribute to, but the thing itself, from high-level architecture down to the implementation.

Design the surface developers live on. Honcho is a developer product. Every API decision is felt immediately by 40,000 people building against it, and ergonomics compound in both directions. You'll be judged on the interfaces as much as the internals.

Own where Honcho meets the ecosystem. Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, and whatever ships next month--every one an upstream we don't control, moving on someone else's release schedule. Your job is straightforward: build, improve, and operate the infrastructure primitives that every service at Chainalysis depends on — Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, streaming infrastructure (Kafka / WarpStream), secrets management, IAM, and the reconcilers that make it all self-service and drift-free. This is an infrastructure-focused IC role at the C4 level, typically suited for someone with 3–5 years of experience. You will work alongside senior engineers who will pair with you, review your work, and invest in your growth. You will report to the Senior Manager of Platform Engineering.

In this role, you'll:

  • Build and maintain cloud infrastructure across AWS and GCP using Terraform — designing the modules and patterns that provision the substrate our services run on, and thinking beyond the immediate use case to how your work is consumed across the organization

  • Operate and evolve multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters (EKS) serving the entire engineering organization — owning node lifecycle, upgrades, security contexts, and networking decisions that affect every team

  • Own the operational side of our streaming infrastructure migration from managed Kafka (MSK) to WarpStream, building and maintaining the tooling that supports it

  • Contribute to platform tooling and reconcilers that underpin our platform contract model — writing Go, working with the Kubernetes API, and building high-quality self-service primitives that engineering teams rely on to declare what their services need

  • Design and maintain foundational networking and security infrastructure — transit gateways, GCP interconnect, ingress, security groups, IAM policies, and IRSA — getting the invisible plumbing right so nobody has to think about it

  • Participate in on-call rotations and drive operational excellence — responding to infrastructure incidents, writing and improving runbooks, and feeding every incident pattern back into automation so the same class of issue never repeats

We're looking for candidates who have:

  • 3+ years of software engineering or infrastructure engineering experience

  • Hands-on experience with AWS services (EC2, EKS, IAM, S3, VPC, or similar) — we're looking for people who have built and operated real infrastructure, not certifications

  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes in production — you have operated or deployed workloads on K8s clusters beyond a local environment

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform strongly preferred; Pulumi or CloudFormation acceptable)

  • Proficiency in at least one of Go, Python, or shell scripting — Go is preferred because our reconciler work is in Go, but you should be ready to turn your hand to whatever the problem demands

  • Comfort with CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Argo, Jenkins, or similar) and hands-on experience with on-call and incident response — you understand what it means to be accountable for production systems

You might also have:

  • Experience building Kubernetes operators or controllers — CRDs, reconcilers, and the controller-runtime library

  • Familiarity with streaming infrastructure (Kafka, WarpStream, or similar event-driven systems) or depth in networking (VPCs, transit gateways, ingress controllers, DNS, load balancing, and security groups)

  • Experience in regulated environments (SOC 2, ISO-27001, or similar compliance frameworks) or familiarity with GitOps patterns (ArgoCD, Flux)

  • A passion for platform engineering as leverage — you care about making other engineers more productive, and when you see toil, your instinct is to eliminate it

Technologies we use:

  • Languages: Go, Python, Bash/Shell, HCL (Terraform)

  • Cloud: AWS (EC2, EKS, IAM, S3, VPC, Lambda), GCP

  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform

  • Kubernetes: EKS, Helm, CRDs, controller-runtime

  • Streaming: Kafka, WarpStream (migrating from MSK)

  • Networking: Transit Gateway, GCP Interconnect, Ingress Controllers, DNS, Security Groups

  • Identity & Security: IAM, IRSA, Secrets Management

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

Rain is hiring a Senior Product Manager to own our onchain surface — the blockchain layer that everything else at Rain depends on. Stablecoins only work as real-world money if the onchain side is fast, safe, and invisible: collateral held in contracts, settlement across chains, custody and wallet architecture, and the asset and network coverage our partners need to operate globally. This role owns that.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll be the directly responsible PM for onchain end to end: smart contracts and protocol design, chain and asset integrations, settlement and treasury flows, and the infrastructure underneath it all. You'll work closely with engineering, security, compliance, legal, and directly with our fintech, neobank, and institutional partners.

  • Own the roadmap for Rain's onchain product — smart contracts, chain and asset coverage, settlement, and payments — and drive it end to end

  • Decide which chains, assets, and stablecoins Rain supports and when — build the framework for those calls across liquidity, security, cost, partner demand, compliance considerations, and regulatory exposure

  • Drive the security bar for onchain work — audits, monitoring, incident response, and the operational guardrails that go with holding real value onchain

  • Translate complex protocol and blockchain infrastructure into intuitive product surfaces and clear partner-facing documentation

  • Gather feedback directly from partners, distill it into sharp prioritization, and push the team toward the highest-leverage work

  • Measure ruthlessly, iterate quickly, and set a bar others want to work to

  • 8-10 years of product management experience, with a track record of shipping products from zero-to-one through scale at a product-led company with a strong engineering culture and high bar for quality

  • Deep, hands-on blockchain fluency — you've shipped onchain products and can reason unaided about EVM and Solana mechanics (and other chains), smart contract design and upgrade patterns, gas economics, bridging models, and other onchain tradeoffs

  • Exceptional product judgment and analytical rigor — you're someone others describe as one of the sharpest PMs they've worked with, and you consistently raise the bar for the people around you

  • A senior, autonomous operator who can define the problem, drive the plan, and own the outcome without needing close direction

  • Sound instincts on onchain security and risk: you know where value gets lost, you push for audits and monitoring before incidents rather than after, and you can weigh a shipping deadline against a real risk without flinching

  • Strong technical fluency beyond the chain itself (APIs, distributed systems, payments and ledger design) and the instinct to pull on technical threads yourself rather than defer to engineering

  • Genuinely excited to live in the details — you believe product quality is won in the specifics and are energized by the work to get them right

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; you can operate with sophisticated external partners and internal engineering teams with equal ease

  • Proven ability to ship quickly, measure adoption, and iterate in a fast-moving environment

NICE TO HAVE, BUT NOT MANDATORY

  • Experience with stablecoin issuance, onchain lending or collateralized credit, or tokenized asset products

  • Background at a protocol, L1/L2, wallet, custodian, or onchain infrastructure company

  • Familiarity with non-EVM ecosystems (Solana, Tron, Bitcoin L2s) and multi-chain operations at scale

  • Experience with payments, card issuing, or cross-border fintech products

  • Working knowledge of the regulatory landscape around digital assets and custody

  • Previous startup or hypergrowth environment experience

About Us

Venice is the world’s leading consumer AI company built on principles of privacy, free speech, and user sovereignty. 

We’re building the Port City of AI, in which millions of individuals, third party apps, and AI agents gather, interact, and access sophisticated AI resources on a private and permissive foundation.  Our mission is to make artificial intelligence approachable and useful in everyday work—bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and practical, real-world impact.

We’re a fast-moving startup where every team member is expected to make a clear impact. Our culture is rooted in curiosity, ownership, ethical principle, philosophy, and collaboration—whether we’re designing better AI workflows, supporting our growing community, or shaping the future of human-AI interaction.

Joining Venice AI means joining a team of unorthodox builders who believe in moving quickly, delivering a beautiful mass-market and highly useful consumer product that doesn’t spy on people or censor their ideas and questions., and maintaining an edge in the rapidly evolving world of agentic machine intelligence. If you’re energized by big ideas, entrepreneurial spirit, individual empowerment, and the opportunity to help shape a fast-growing company in the world’s hottest industry from the ground up, please reach out.you’ll feel right at home here.

Why We’re Hiring

Venice is growing fast! Every day we are shipping new products, expanding into new modalities, and making decisions that shape the future of the platform. We know that to make the right decisions, they need to be grounded in data. 

Venice is a privacy-first company, which means we deliberately collect less user data than most companies in our space. We don’t track what we don’t need and we don’t store what we shouldn’t. This is a core part of who we are, and it’s not negotiable.

This creates a real analytical challenge: How do you inform business insights when you have limited user data? How do you make confident product decisions when you have less data than your competitors? How do you separate signal from noise without the crutch of exhaustive user tracking?

To help us answer these questions, we’re hiring a Senior Data Scientist who operates as a tactical analytics leader to be the authoritative source on data at Venice. You will own where data is sourced from, where it is stored, how it is accessed and how it is queried. You will build the systems and provide the answers the business needs, with oversight, auditability, and clean code. You’ll be the person who not only bridges the gap between our privacy principles and our need for rigorous, data-driven product decisions, but also who proactively surfaces the strategic questions leadership hasn’t asked yet - anticipating what matters to the business. You will know the data like the back of your hand. 

We don’t want someone fighting the privacy model; we want someone to successfully work within it. 

This role will report to the VP of Business Operations and will work closely with product managers, engineering, finance, marketing and the leadership team. Your job is to ensure that every major business and product decision is backed by analysis that’s both rigorous and honest about its limitations.

What You’ll Do

Own the data, end to end. Decide where data lives, how it flows, and how it's queried. Build the infrastructure, tooling, and dashboards that make you the expert on company data, from raw sourcing through to the insights that shape business and product decisions. Everyone should be able to point to your work as the ground truth.

Consolidate data access. Ensure the business accesses data consistently - including financial statements, product metrics, and growth analysis. No isolated islands, no duplicate systems. Build a shared data lake with specialized views on top.

Support experiment tracking. While experimentation strategy lives with Product, you will help track experiments, building the systems so Product can monitor tests without managing spreadsheets.

Ask and answer strategic questions about the business and our products. Be honest about uncertainty. You proactively identify what questions will be asked and bring answers to the table with analysis. You won’t have the luxury of exhaustive telemetry. You’ll need to be creative: derive insights from the data we do have, use statistical methods that work with small samples, and be transparent about confidence levels. When the data isn’t enough to be certain, say so. Recommend the decision anyway, with appropriate caveats. False certainty is worse than acknowledged uncertainty.

Build the analytical foundation. We have an internal data warehouse and product analytics tooling. You’ll assess what’s there, identify gaps, and build what’s missing. This might include dashboards, self-serve analysis tools for product managers, data models, and reporting pipelines. The goal: make analytics accessible to decision-makers without requiring them to come to you for every question.

Partner across the org. You bring insights to internal stakeholders to guide and reshape roadmaps. Work with engineering to instrument products thoughtfully: collecting what’s needed for decisions without collecting what isn’t. Work with finance on business metrics. Work with marketing on growth attribution. Work with the executive team on company-level metrics and strategic questions.

Protect the privacy line. Be the analytical voice that says “we don’t need to collect this” when new tracking is proposed. Help the team understand the tradeoff between data granularity and user trust. Find analytical methods that don’t require invasive tracking. This is not about blocking progress; it’s about finding the path that keeps both the product and the principles intact.

Separate signal from noise in a fast-moving product. Venice ships constantly. New models, new features, new modalities, new revenue streams. You’ll need to build metrics that are robust to this pace of change, and help the team distinguish real trends from noise when the product is evolving week over week.

*We retain the right to change or assign other duties to this position.

Who You Are

You're a product-minded data leader with engineering depth. You have 7+ years of demonstrated experience, but you’re not just a technical executor, you think like a product manager and business owner first. You understand that the goal is better decisions, not more dashboards. You surface the questions that matter and can translate a business question into an analysis and put forth a recommendation. You think about the API funnel, where users come from, and conversion. You've worked in environments where data is messy, incomplete, or deliberately constrained, and you find creative ways through it: quasi-experiments, proxy metrics, qualitative triangulation, and decision frameworks that work with what you have.

You can work in the DB and partner with Engineering to influence robust data systems. You write production-quality code, you're fluent in SQL, and you can build data pipelines, models, and tooling that become infrastructure. You understand data warehousing concepts and have worked with modern analytics stacks. Venice's stack includes Rust, TypeScript, Go, and Python; familiarity with more than one is a plus. You have experience with PostHog for product analytics and Postgres for data storage and querying, and you understand PostHog's potential as a central platform across error tracking, support, and conversation data.

You communicate clearly, especially about uncertainty. You can present to the executive team without hiding behind jargon. You're honest about what the data shows and what it doesn't. You don't overclaim. You can say "I'm 70% confident in this direction" and explain what would change your mind. You help decision-makers act under uncertainty rather than wait for certainty that won't come.

You respect the privacy mission. You understand why Venice collects less data than competitors, and you agree with it. You're not looking for ways to work around the constraint. You're looking for ways to make great decisions within it. You've thought about the ethics of data collection and have opinions about what companies should and shouldn't track.

You move fast and iterate. You prefer a rough analysis this week that informs a decision over a perfect model next month that's too late. You iterate on methods and tooling in production. You identify what’s needed, advocate for it, and see it through. You're also excited about using AI agents as part of your workflow: leveraging LLMs to accelerate analysis, automate repetitive data work, and surface insights faster. You see agents as a tool that makes you more productive, not a threat to the analytical craft.

Sapien is building Proof of Quality, an evaluation system for AI work

As AI moves from generating answers to doing real work, teams need confidence in the quality of everything their AI systems rely on and produce.

AI work includes the data going in, the reasoning in the middle, the outputs coming back, and the decisions and actions agents take. Quality matters at every step.

Proof of Quality, or PoQ, measures that work against the customer's own standard.

The customer's rubric defines quality. Agents handle the volume. Qualified experts judge what requires judgment. Consensus turns independent assessments into a measure reliable enough to act on.

Every evaluation produces a record the customer keeps. Teams can see what passed, what failed, why, and what needs to improve.

We've spent two years and 195 million tasks learning how hard it is to measure quality at scale.

Now we're hiring our first dedicated sales lead to take PoQ to market.

Why now

AI made work abundant. Judgment did not scale with it.

Models are becoming agents. Agents are moving into production. AI systems increasingly depend on complex data, perform multi-step reasoning, generate open ended work, and make decisions that affect real products and workflows.

Some quality can be checked automatically. Much of it depends on context, expertise, or judgment.

The answer cannot be to put an expert behind every piece of AI work.

Reliable judgment needs a process, and scarce expertise has to be deployed where it actually adds value.

That is the problem PoQ is built to solve.

You'll join while this market is taking shape, with direct access to the founders, meaningful ownership, and the opportunity to help define how PoQ reaches it.

The role

You'll own sales end to end: prospecting, discovery, demos, pilots, pricing, negotiation, and close.

Sales today is founder led. We've opened the first doors, run the first demos, and learned where PoQ gets the strongest reaction.

Your job is to take that baseline and build from it.

There is no proven ICP to inherit.

We have strong hypotheses and early signals, but we're still mapping the buyers, use cases, segments, and price points where PoQ has the strongest pull.

That means you're selling and discovering the market at the same time.

Revenue matters. So does signal.

Every customer conversation should make us smarter about:

  • who feels the problem most acutely
  • what AI work they need confidence in
  • where quality is easy to test and where judgment becomes necessary
  • what gets them to run a pilot
  • what they will pay
  • which objections repeat
  • what they compare us to
  • where PoQ clearly wins, and where it does not

Your job is to run enough good conversations to find those patterns quickly, turn the strongest ones into pilots and revenue, and feed what you learn back into product, pricing, and positioning.

This is not a role where you inherit a mature pipeline and execute an established playbook.

If you need a locked pitch deck, settled price book, and fixed ICP before you can sell, this is probably the wrong role.

If discovering the market while selling into it sounds like the fun part, keep reading.

Credibility matters

You'll often be selling to technical buyers: AI labs, agent companies, data teams, and engineering leaders.

You should be able to run a technical demo yourself, understand the buyer's problem beyond the surface level, and handle the second and third question, not just the first.

Your outbound should sound like you understand the company you're writing to.

You should know when bringing in a founder or engineer materially improves a deal, and when you should handle it yourself.

And you should be comfortable disqualifying quickly when there isn't a real fit.

We care more about strong conversations that create real signal and business than a CRM full of polite meetings.

Who this is for

We care more about what you've actually done than where you've worked.

You don't need ten years of enterprise sales or a famous logo on your résumé.

You do need evidence that you can create opportunities and close them.

You'll likely be a strong fit if you:

  • have personally sourced and closed real business
  • are comfortable selling technical products to technical buyers
  • are excellent at discovery and getting to the real customer problem
  • use AI tools heavily in your daily work
  • think in numbers and patterns
  • work quickly and independently
  • are comfortable operating without a rigid sales playbook
  • can turn customer feedback into useful signal for product and positioning

Experience in AI, data, developer tools, infrastructure, or crypto is a strong plus.

What you'll own

Market discovery

Build a steady flow of qualified customer conversations through outbound, networks, communities, and other channels.

The goal isn't activity for its own sake. It's enough high quality market contact to learn quickly where PoQ has real pull.

Volume matters, but so does relevance. Your outreach should feel informed because it is.

Sales, end to end

Own the deal from first conversation through discovery, demo, pilot, negotiation, and signed customer.

Bring in founders and engineers when they materially improve the deal.

Pilots

Get strong prospects into useful pilots quickly.

PoQ pilots run in days rather than quarters. The rubric, panel, expected effort, and cost are defined up front, and the first Proof Report lands while the decision it informs is still open.

You'll help define success, keep pilots moving, and turn successful ones into customers, references, case studies, and expansion opportunities.

Pilots are commercial opportunities, but they are also one of the fastest ways for us to learn where PoQ creates the most value.

ICP and pricing

Treat every conversation as data.

Track use cases, objections, pricing reactions, buyer profiles, and why deals move or stall.

Use that information to sharpen our ICP, positioning, packaging, and pricing.

You'll help decide where PoQ wins, not just sell where you're told.

Network

Make intelligent use of Sapien's existing network of founders, investors, advisors, partners, and communities.

Turn warm introductions into a repeatable channel rather than an advantage spent once.

Sales operations

Own the CRM, pipeline, forecast, and the systems required to understand what's working.

Every stage should be visible. Every meaningful conversion rate should be known.

As the motion becomes repeatable, you'll help shape the sales team we build around it.

What we look for

Proof over polish.

Show us deals, pilots, partnerships, or revenue you personally helped create.

We want to understand:

  • where the opportunity started
  • what you personally owned
  • what made the deal difficult
  • what the result was
  • what the numbers looked like

We also expect:

  • daily fluency with tools like ChatGPT and Claude
  • strong research and prospecting instincts
  • enough technical aptitude to learn PoQ deeply and demo it credibly
  • comfort with modern CRM, sequencing, enrichment, and automation tools
  • a habit of measuring what works and changing what doesn't
  • speed

How you'll be measured

This role has a scoreboard, but it isn't just revenue.

Targets will be set together each quarter and evolve as we learn. They'll fall into four areas:

1. Qualified conversations. Are you consistently creating conversations with companies that have a real reason to buy?

2. Pilots. Are strong prospects moving into structured evaluations of PoQ?

3. Revenue. Are pilots and conversations turning into paying customers?

4. Market signal. Are we learning faster because of the conversations you're running? Are those insights changing who we target, what we build, how we price, or how we position PoQ?

If those numbers and signals improve quarter over quarter, you're succeeding.

Your first 90 days

By the end of your first 90 days, we expect you to have:

  • learned PoQ well enough to sell and demo it independently
  • absorbed the customer conversations and sales work already done
  • launched and iterated on your own outbound motion
  • built a meaningful pipeline of qualified opportunities
  • moved multiple strong prospects toward or into pilots
  • developed an evidence backed view of which segments, buyers, and use cases show the strongest pull
  • made meaningful commercial progress toward a repeatable sales motion

We expect speed, but we care more about learning the market correctly than manufacturing activity.

How to apply

Send us your résumé plus two or three examples of deals or pipelines you actually built.

For each, tell us:

  • the starting point
  • the result
  • the timeframe
  • what you personally owned

Screenshots of pipelines, sequences, dashboards, or other real work are welcome.

Then do one more thing:

Pick a company you think should buy Proof of Quality. Tell us why, and write the exact outbound you'd send them.

That matters more to us than a polished cover letter.

Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Wave is now the largest financial institution in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire, with millions of users, growing rapidly year-on-year. And, we’re still in the early days of our product roadmap and potential impact on people’s everyday lives.

As an Observability Engineer at Wave, you will help engineers understand, operate, debug, and improve the systems that power payments for millions of users across Africa.

You will own and evolve Wave’s observability platform across our Python backend, GraphQL API, Postgres and CockroachDB databases, Kubernetes workloads, cloud infrastructure, and on-premises environments. Your work will make it easier for product, database, infrastructure, and security teams to detect problems and regressions early, understand system behaviour, resolve incidents quickly, and make well-informed reliability and performance decisions.

You'll work in the newly formed Performance & Observability team and report to the Director of Platform. You'll partner closely with infrastructure, database, and product engineering teams to improve how we instrument our services.

In this role you'll:

  • Improve our understanding of production behaviour across application code, GraphQL APIs, databases, caches, Kubernetes workloads, cloud infrastructure, async jobs, and on-premises environments.
  • Partner with product and platform teams to define meaningful service-level indicators, reduce alert fatigue, and ensure alerts are actionable, reliable, and tied to user impact.
  • Build internal tooling and self-service workflows that help engineers instrument services, investigate incidents, analyse performance, and understand dependencies.
  • Help teams identify reliability, latency, capacity, and cost issues before they become user-facing incidents.
  • Establish and implement observability standards, documentation, and training materials that scale across Wave’s engineering organisation.
  • Operate and improve our observability platform (e.g., Datadog, Honeycomb, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) while controlling costs as data volume grows.

You might be a good fit if you...

  • Care a lot about working on software whose mission you can believe in.
  • Have a bias for action. You see a problem, you fix a problem. You get buy-in for your solutions and keep work moving.
  • Approach your work with a growth mindset and use your skills and experience to mentor less-experienced engineers.
  • Are excited to build world-class infrastructure that powers economic opportunity for an entire continent.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in observability, SRE, platform engineering, infrastructure engineering, backend engineering, or production systems engineering.
  • Deep understanding of metrics, logging, tracing, profiling, alerting, dashboards, service-level indicators, and incident response workflows at scale.
  • Experience building internal tools, libraries, automation, or platforms used by other engineers.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills. This role succeeds by helping other engineers build, operate, and debug better systems.
  • Pragmatic judgment about when to improve tooling, when to simplify, and when to avoid unnecessary complexity.
  • Experience learning, analyzing, and working on other people’s code.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in at least one backend language, preferably Python.
  • Experience with observability tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Tempo, Loki, Honeycomb, Sentry, or similar systems.
  • Experience with at least some our stack, Postgres, CockroachDB, Redis, GraphQL, or Kubernetes.
  • Experience with OpenTelemetry instrumentation and collector configuration at scale

About the Performance & Observability Team

The Performance and Observability team was recently formed with the hiring of our first performance engineer, and is expanding with this Observability position. The team is and will continue to define its scope. The observability scope within the team currently is:

  • Ownership, management and evolution of observability tools: Datadog, Honeycomb, Sentry, and Pyroscope.
  • Design of SLOs and support product teams in implementing them.
  • Support all teams in improving their alert quality.
  • Ownership of observability modules and code, ensuring consistent naming conventions across all our systems.

Some recent and potential projects, as examples of specific things the team has worked on:

  • Early detection of regressions in our code. This could be a performance, reliability, or other regression that impacts our users.
  • CPU profiling in production.
  • SLO support for product teams.
  • Scaling our Observability platform to support 4x our current volume while keeping costs in check.

About engineering at Wave

We care about the big picture. We don’t hire engineers to just ship tickets. We hire them to solve problems. That means caring deeply about outcomes, understanding context, and jumping in wherever something’s broken, even if it’s technically “not your area.” When we see problems, inefficiencies, or opportunities to make something better, we act. We dig into operational issues, clarify fuzzy product specs, or step into unfamiliar code to help unblock teammates.

We move as fast as possible. Speed matters. It lets us try things quickly, get feedback early, and course-correct while it’s cheap. So we write small PRs. We aim for MVPs. We leave TODOs and file follow-ups. We don’t over-perfect v1. That said, we’re building a financial product. Some things—like money movement, correctness, or security—deserve more caution.

We like boring technology. We favor tools that are reliable, well-understood, and easy to debug. This keeps us focused on solving meaningful problems instead of wrestling with unpredictable infrastructure. If a new technology helps us move faster, build safer, or solve a real need, we’ll consider it. But we don’t adopt tools just because they’re new—we adopt them because they’re right.

Simplicity is a strategy. It lets us focus our energy where it matters most: serving our users.

OVERVIEW

Modern Treasury is hiring a Head of Risk to build our risk function from the ground up. Money moves through Modern Treasury for some of the largest and fastest-growing companies in the economy. How well we manage the risk in that movement directly shapes the product — who we can onboard, how fast they can transact, and how much friction they feel along the way.

This is a foundational, hands-on role. You will decide how customers are underwritten, how limits and reserves are set, how transactions are authorized, and how we detect fraud — and you will build those systems early, before scale forces the decisions for you.

This role reports to our General Counsel, who leads Legal, Compliance, and Risk.

ABOUT MODERN TREASURY

Modern Treasury provides trusted infrastructure for money movement. The company helps teams launch and scale payment experiences in days, not months. With best-in-class developer tools and a single API for fiat and stablecoins, plus built-in compliance, ledgering, and reporting, Modern Treasury enables businesses to move money instantly, reliably, and at scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will start as an individual contributor with the mandate to build. You will own:

  • Onboarding & underwriting: How we evaluate customers before they move money with us — what we need to know to say yes, what conditions we attach, and how to reach that decision fast enough that it isn't the reason a customer picks someone else. You will partner with Compliance on KYB while owning the underwriting judgment beside it.

  • Transaction risk & limits: How we authorize money movement in real time, and how limits flex as we learn more about a business. This includes the hard cases — managing dynamic limits when a few customers drive most of the volume, and loosening constraints on good customers as fast as the data allows.

  • Reserves & exposure: Reserve policy and our view of loss exposure across ACH returns, unauthorized debits, and counterparty failure. You will quantify what we're exposed to, decide what's worth taking, and make that reasoning legible to the rest of the company.

  • Detection & the risk engine: The machinery. You will select and deploy the tooling — vendor, in-house, or both — that turns policy into automated decisions, and use modern AI tooling to automate case handling rather than staffing your way out of the problem.

  • New rails, stablecoins & wallet controls: The emerging surface area. You will help Modern Treasury expand into stablecoins, wallets, RfP, and local rails in other countries safely — understanding the risks unique to each rail, partnering with Product on controls that are both safe and usable, and designing for new money-movement patterns before they become edge cases at scale.

You will work across Engineering, Product, Compliance, Finance, and our customer-facing teams, and make sure risk and compliance run on one coherent set of systems rather than two stacks that disagree.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • You've built this before: You've stood up a risk function at an early-stage or high-growth company rather than inherited a mature one. You know what the first version looks like, what to defer, and what will hurt in eighteen months if you skip it now.

  • Payments risk, specifically: Not lending or credit. You understand ACH returns, settlement timing, unauthorized debit exposure, and counterparty risk. You know the difference between risk and compliance, and where they have to work as one.

  • Curiosity about new rails: Stablecoin, wallet, RfP, or international local-rail experience is a strong plus. More importantly, you are interested in learning unfamiliar rails quickly and translating their unique risks into practical product and operational controls.

  • A systems thinker, not a queue operator: You think about decisioning at scale and design for an order of magnitude more volume. You'll set thresholds and review edge cases by hand when needed, but you're building toward something that doesn't require it.

  • Technical and data fluency: You can go deep with engineers and hold your own. You're comfortable in the data yourself — SQL, ideally Python — and fluent in applying modern AI tools to operational problems.

  • Scar tissue, earned well: You've seen things go wrong — a fraud ring, a loss event, a control that failed in a way nobody anticipated — and carry the pattern recognition that comes with it. You were in the room, not the cause.

  • Judgment you can defend: You'll make consequential calls with incomplete information and get some wrong. You reason clearly about tradeoffs, write your thinking down, and can explain why a decision was right even when the outcome wasn't.

  • Influence across the company: You'll often be telling people something they don't want to hear. You can make the case for risk investment in terms the rest of the business cares about.

  • Management experience is a plus: You may hire onto this team within the first year. You don't need to have run a large org, but you should have managed before and want to build a team over time.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking its first dedicated Financial Crimes Compliance Controls Senior Strategist to build and own the framework that demonstrates FCC controls are working as intended, remain effective as risk evolves, and can be clearly supported in bank-partner, audit, and regulatory examinations.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the intersection of financial-crimes compliance, controls effectiveness, technology, data, and AI-enabled operations. You will serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for program-level Product, Engineering, Design, and Data (“PEDD”) initiatives, ensuring FCC requirements, controls, and risk considerations are incorporated into strategic product and technology planning. This role complements the broader team’s cross-functional partnerships by focusing specifically on major PEDD-led initiatives.

This is a builder role for an experienced financial-crimes compliance professional with deep analytical skills and strong BSA/AML, and sanctions subject-matter expertise You will assess emerging and existing financial-crimes risks, make sound and defensible control decisions, and help build the processes, technology partnerships, and governance needed for FCC to scale responsibly. Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

 

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.

Location

  • Remote – Europe or US (EST only)

  • Hybrid – Paris or New York

 

Role

Morpho's GTM motion has grown faster than the operations behind it. Pipeline visibility, CRM hygiene, forecasting, and tooling are split across people who all have other jobs, and nobody owns the end-to-end picture. This role owns RevOps outright and builds the systems that help the GTM team close more relevant deals, faster.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own GTM dashboards and KPI reporting so the team tracks what matters and trusts the numbers.

  • Run the GTM tech stack, automations, and AI tooling to keep business developers fast and well informed.

  • Keep the CRM minimal and clean, with stages, hygiene, and processes people actually follow.

  • Build business intelligence and forecasting to set targets that are ambitious and credible, and to spot new trends early.

  • Surface signals from markets and media so business developers can chase, upsell, and close at the right moment.

  • Track rep attribution, productivity, quotas, and territories to keep the team accountable and improving.

  • Own the knowledge base and data management so accurate information is easy to find and reuse.

 

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days

  • You are fully up to speed on the Morpho product, protocol, and roadmap, and you understand how the GTM team operates today.

  • You have a prioritized plan for what to build, fix, and delete, and you are already making reps faster.

 

First 3 months

  • You have fixed the biggest gaps and bottlenecks: a cleaner CRM, simpler processes, and the automations, dashboards, and forecasts business developers rely on daily.

  • You are central to productivity assessment, rep attribution, and deal tracking.

 

First 6 months

  • You own the full RevOps stack and bridge GTM and Finance.

  • Leadership has full visibility into the business to make better decisions, and you lead entire projects end to end.

 

Must Have Skills & Experience

  • DeFi native: you use onchain products and understand how protocols and their users behave.

  • Experience as a RevOps, growth engineer, or business analyst at a B2B startup.

  • Tech or software background: comfortable building automations and reasoning about connected systems.

  • Strong with data: cleaning, modeling, analyzing, and reporting it accurately.

  • Business mindset with a critical eye: you challenge metrics and simplify by default.

  • Strong ownership and autonomy: doesn't wait to be told.

  • Clear and crisp async communication.

  • Comfort operating in fast-changing, ambiguous contexts.

  • Team-first mindset, low ego.

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

 

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.

About the Role

Hi, I'm Dan Davidow, Chief Marketing Officer at Jane. I joined Jane because I have a real passion for helping small businesses succeed, and our customers run some of the most impactful small businesses there are. When I'm not doing that, you'll usually find me planning my next trip.

Jane has built strong momentum, and our next phase of growth will be driven by deeper relationships, trusted partnerships, and a strong presence in the healthcare community. We have also found success in our demand gen programs, and now is the time to build on what's already working.

That's where you come in. As our Director of SMB & Self Serve Demand Generation, you'll own a core part of how Jane generates demand: our paid media program, our website (including SEO and AEO), and our lifecycle marketing. You'll work alongside the teams who own events, partnerships, and community, so that together it all adds up to one cohesive motion. AI is central to how you'll do this: from how practitioners discover Jane through AI-driven search, to how we use AI to plan, build, and optimize our own programs. You’ll also partner closely with our growth product team who works on onboarding and optimizing user flow.

You'll lead a team of three channel experts today, with room to grow the team as the program scales, and partner closely with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team on measurement and infrastructure.

This is a role for a leader who can balance strategy and execution. Part of this job is hands-on; you're comfortable working directly in the campaigns, data and tools, and building AI-assisted workflows yourself, not just directing from above. Success looks like building trust with our market and driving real business impact.

 

What Impact We’re Looking for You to Make

  • Own paid media. Lead our paid media budget and team across channels, including paid search, paid social, direct mail, and more - deciding where we invest, how we measure it, and when we shift.

  • Partner with Growth Product. You’ll work directly with designers, developers, and product managers building the future of onboarding and activation at Jane, designing and executing thoughtful tests.

  • Deliver on web experience. Manage the marketing side of jane.com - the front door to Jane for practitioners, patients, and the broader healthcare community. Partner closely with design and engineering, and own site strategy, conversion rate, and our organic presence across both traditional search (SEO) and AI-driven discovery (AEO).

  • Own lifecycle marketing. Design and run the programs that guide practitioners from first touch through trial, signup, and expansion, working closely with product marketing and sales on what happens at each stage.

  • Put AI to work. Make Jane easy to find in an AI-first world, and use AI across the demand program itself - research, creative testing, campaign optimization, reporting - so a small team can operate like a much bigger one.

  • Sharpen our measurement. We have a solid measurement foundation today. You'll define what the demand program needs next - KPIs, attribution, reporting - and partner with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team to build it.

  • Align with Sales and Support. Work deeply with our sales and support teams to design demand programs that support revenue outcomes, not just top-of-page metrics.

  • Build the team. Lead, coach, and grow a team of channel experts, and raise the bar on how we plan, test, and learn together.

 

What Experience We Need

  • A strong track record in demand gen or growth marketing. 5-7 years driving tangible business impact, ideally with experience managing and scaling multi-million-dollar budgets.

  • Deeply analytical. Exceptional at translating numbers into marketing strategy, and comfortable operating in a constrained, highly data-driven environment. Deep expertise across marketing analytics, web optimization, lifecycle, and paid acquisition.

  • High-velocity SMB experience. Proven success in high-velocity business models, ideally SMB or consumer. We're not looking for someone whose experience is only account-based marketing or traditional enterprise SaaS.

  • A builder of teams. A track record of hiring and developing high-caliber growth marketing talent.

Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company born in North Vancouver, British Columbia. We're now a team of more than 900 people working remotely across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. Polymarket is looking for an Infrastructure Engineer to help build, scale, and operate the platform that our exchange and product engineering teams run on. This role is focused on the systems underneath the systems — Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and reliability — that let our engineers ship fast without breaking things.

You'll be a core individual contributor working with senior engineers across the org to design, automate, and harden the infrastructure that powers Polymarket at scale. This is a high-ownership role with minimal bureaucracy and a strong bias toward execution.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Docker in production — cluster operations, workload orchestration, and container lifecycle management.
